literature.headline_zh: 季节性流感病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期季节性流感病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 蒿提取物显着抑制 H1N1pdm09 和 H3N2 病毒复制,在感染细胞中观察到病毒滴度降低 70%,并显示出对 TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB 信号通路的显着调节。 [10.3390/ph19081170]
主要结论是,在“同一个健康”框架下加强兽医 监测 可以改善病毒重配事件的检测,增强病毒传播的可追溯性,并支持集约化畜牧系统的及时风险评估。台湾的经验表明,将分子流行病学、兽医现场监测和跨部门沟通相结合,为流行病防范提供了实用价值。 [10.1007/s11259-026-11411-0]
与大流行前相比,大流行后 6 个月 17 岁和 18-64 岁儿童中针对 甲型H3N2流感病毒 和乙型流感的 VE 显着升高。相反,大流行后 18-64 岁人群中 VE 相对于 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 的水平较低。≥65 岁的人群没有观察到显着差异,并且 B/维多利亚数据有限。 [10.1016/j.vaccine.2026.128956]
结果表明,B/Yamagata 的灭绝主要是由于其较低的基本繁殖数,使其在大流行的早期阶段特别脆弱,而 B/Victoria 在同一时期勉强避免了灭绝。 [10.64898/2026.07.22.26358639]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Of the 4694 enrolled elderly patients with ILI, 1587 (33.81%) were influenza-positive, with A(H1N1)pdm09 being the dominant subtype (93.3%). Vaccination coverage was 32.72% (1536/4694). [10.1186/s12877-026-08049-7]

Artemisia extracts significantly suppressed H1N1pdm09 and H3N2 viral replication, with a 70% reduction in viral titers observed in infected cells, and demonstrated a notable modulation of the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling pathway. [10.3390/ph19081170]

The key conclusion is that strengthened veterinary surveillance under a One Health framework can improve the detection of viral reassortment events, enhance traceability of viral spread, and support timely risk assessment in intensive livestock systems. [10.1007/s11259-026-11411-0]

Post-pandemic VE against A(H3N2) and influenza B was significantly higher in 6-month-17-year-olds and 18-64-year-olds compared to pre-pandemic. Conversely, VE against A(H1N1)pdm09 was lower post-pandemic in 18-64-year-olds. No significant differences were observed for ≥65-year-olds, and B/Victoria data were limited. [10.1016/j.vaccine.2026.128956]

The results indicate that B/Yamagata's extinction was mainly driven by its lower basic reproduction number, making it particularly vulnerable during the early phase of the pandemic, while B/Victoria narrowly avoided extinction during the same period. [10.64898/2026.07.22.26358639]

papers.title: Molecular Surveillance and Genomic Characterization of Influenza A(H3N2) Viruses From a Secondary‐Care Surveillance Site in Pakistan During the 2025–2026 Winter Season
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Respiratory viral infections, particularly Influenza A and SARS‐CoV‐2, remain major public health concerns in endemic settings such as Pakistan, where high influenza‐like illness burden and limited genomic data underscore the need for surveillance to guide vaccine strategies. This study assessed respiratory virus circulation and genetic diversity among ILI cases at a secondary‐care hospital in Islamabad during the 2025–2026 winter season. Among 170 qRT‐PCR‐tested cases, Influenza A was detected in 24.1%, SARS‐CoV‐2 in 1.17%, and Influenza B was not detected. Influenza A positivity was slightly higher in females (25.0%), with highest burden in individuals aged 11–20 years. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道病毒感染,特别是甲型流感和 SARS-CoV-2,仍然是巴基斯坦等流行地区的主要公共卫生问题,那里的高流感样疾病负担和有限的基因组数据强调需要 监测 来指导 疫苗 策略。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究评估了 2025 年至 2026 年冬季伊斯兰堡一家二级护理医院流感样病例中的呼吸道病毒传播和遗传多样性。
elements_zh.methods: 在 170 例 qRT-PCR 检测病例中,甲型流感检出率为 24.1%,SARS-CoV-2 检出率为 1.17%,未检出乙型流感。对 21 种流感 甲型H3N2流感病毒 分离株的全 基因组 测序显示,亚支 K (52.4%)、J.2.2 (28.6%) 和 J.2 (9.5%) 存在共循环。
elements_zh.main_results: 女性甲型流感阳性率略高(25.0%),11-20 岁人群的负担最高。系统发育分析显示,亚进化枝 K 与来自北美、大洋洲、欧洲和 WHO 推荐的 2026-2027 年北半球 H3N2 疫苗 菌株的最新分离株聚类,而 J.2 和 J.2.2 与早期的 疫苗 样菌株一致。NA 分析显示分支 B.4.2.2 与 K 谱系相关以及与最近的北美菌株相关性的优势。亚进化枝 K 表现出保守的 HA 取代(K2N、S144N、N158D、I160K、Q173R、T328A)和变化有限的 HA2 S49N。未检测到 抗病毒药物 抗性 突变。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 总体而言,研究结果证明了 H3N2 亚支 K 的优势和遗传稳定性,并支持连续 基因组监测 用于 疫苗 菌株选择和流感准备。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果通过显示 K 分支与 WHO 推荐菌株的一致性来为 疫苗 菌株选择提供信息,并强调 基因组监测 在流感防范中的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在一家二级保健医院进行的,限制了普遍性。然而,由于全面的基因组分析和直接检测方法,证据强度很高。

analysis_zh.main_results: 女性甲型流感阳性率略高(25.0%),11-20 岁人群的负担最高。系统发育分析显示,亚进化枝 K 与来自北美、大洋洲、欧洲和 WHO 推荐的 2026-2027 年北半球 H3N2 疫苗 菌株的最新分离株聚类,而 J.2 和 J.2.2 与早期的 疫苗 样菌株一致。NA 分析显示分支 B.4.2.2 与 K 谱系相关以及与最近的北美菌株相关性的优势。亚进化枝 K 表现出保守的 HA 取代(K2N、S144N、N158D、I160K、Q173R、T328A)和变化有限的 HA2 S49N。未检测到 抗病毒药物 抗性 突变。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 总体而言,研究结果证明了 H3N2 亚支 K 的优势和遗传稳定性,并支持连续 基因组监测 用于 疫苗 菌株选择和流感准备。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果通过显示 K 分支与 WHO 推荐菌株的一致性来为 疫苗 菌株选择提供信息,并强调 基因组监测 在流感防范中的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在一家二级保健医院进行的,限制了普遍性。然而,由于全面的基因组分析和直接检测方法,证据强度很高。

papers.title: Evolution of swine influenza surveillance and one health governance in Taiwan: from zoonotic risk management to integrated preparedness.
papers.abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) remain a persistent global threat because of rapid antigenic change, frequent genetic reassortment, and cross-species transmission. Swine act as key “mixing vessels,” permitting co-infection with avian and human strains and accelerating viral diversification and zoonotic risk. Effective veterinary surveillance is therefore critical for detecting viral evolution within swine populations and for providing early warning at the animal–human interface. Taiwan, home to approximately 5.5 million pigs and 23.4 million people, offers a representative case for examining how swine influenza surveillance has evolved in response to these challenges. This review describes the development of veterinary surveillance strategies from fragmented, event-driven monitoring to a coordinated One Health governance framework incorporating routine whole-genome sequencing, targeted serological surveillance, and coordinated data exchange across sectors. Key historical milestones include mass vaccination and culling programs, the 2009 pandemic response and recent zoonotic detections of H1N2v in humans (2021–2023), collectively evidencing ongoing bidirectional viral exchange. Episodes of severe human seasonal influenza activity, including H3N2-associated outbreaks, further highlighted the importance of coordinated surveillance across human and animal health sectors. By focusing on surveillance practices applied to animals, this review highlights the practical value of integrating molecular epidemiology, veterinary field monitoring, artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled technologies and cross-sector communication under a One Health framework. The Taiwanese experience demonstrates how strengthened veterinary surveillance can improve the sensitivity for detecting reassortment events, enhance traceability of viral spread, and support timely risk assessment in intensive livestock systems. These lessons offer a practical, replicable pathway for other countries aiming to overcome swine influenza surveillance fragmentation and strengthen pandemic preparedness under a One Health framework. The review traces Taiwan’s surveillance evolution from fragmented monitoring of swine influenza A viruses to a coordinated One Health governance model. A(H1N1)pdm09 and human H1N2v infections exposed gaps in notification capacity. The surveillance systems, genome sequencing and AI-enabled analytics are established to link animal, human, and environmental health for pandemic preparedness.

papers.title_original: Evolution of swine influenza surveillance and one health governance in Taiwan: from zoonotic risk management to integrated preparedness.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review examines the evolution of swine influenza surveillance and One Health governance in Taiwan, focusing on the pathogen influenza A viruses (IAVs), the host swine populations, and the population context of Taiwan with 5.5 million pigs and 23.4 million people. The central question is how swine influenza surveillance has evolved from fragmented monitoring to a coordinated One Health framework to address zoonotic risks and pandemic preparedness.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a review article that describes the development of veterinary surveillance strategies in Taiwan, including the transition from fragmented, event-driven monitoring to a coordinated One Health governance framework. The review incorporates routine whole-genome sequencing, targeted serological surveillance, and coordinated data exchange across sectors, as well as the use of AI-enabled technologies for pandemic preparedness.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The key conclusion is that strengthened veterinary surveillance under a One Health framework can improve the detection of viral reassortment events, enhance traceability of viral spread, and support timely risk assessment in intensive livestock systems. The Taiwanese experience demonstrates that integrating molecular epidemiology, veterinary field monitoring, and cross-sector communication provides practical value for pandemic preparedness.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies gaps in notification capacity exposed by A(H1N1)pdm09 and human H1N2v infections. While the surveillance systems have been established to link animal, human, and environmental health, the review does not specify any remaining controversies or unresolved mechanisms, focusing instead on the evolution and benefits of the integrated approach.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The implications highlight the practical value of integrating molecular epidemiology, veterinary field monitoring, AI-enabled technologies, and cross-sector communication under a One Health framework. The Taiwanese experience offers a replicable pathway for other countries to overcome swine influenza surveillance fragmentation and strengthen pandemic preparedness, emphasizing the importance of coordinated surveillance across human and animal health sectors.

Key milestones include mass vaccination, pandemic responses, and zoonotic detections of H1N2v, demonstrating bidirectional viral exchange. The integration of whole-genome sequencing, serological surveillance, and AI technologies under One Health has improved detection of reassortment events and viral traceability. The findings offer a practical, replicable model for other countries to enhance pandemic preparedness by overcoming surveillance fragmentation and fostering cross-sector coordination.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这是一篇评论文章,描述了台湾兽医 监测 战略的发展,包括从分散的、事件驱动的监测到协调的 One Health 治理框架的转变。该审查包括常规全 基因组 测序、靶向血清学 监测 和跨部门的协调数据交换,以及使用人工智能技术进行大流行防范。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 主要结论是,在“同一个健康”框架下加强兽医 监测 可以改善病毒重配事件的检测,增强病毒传播的可追溯性,并支持集约化畜牧系统的及时风险评估。台湾的经验表明,将分子流行病学、兽医现场监测和跨部门沟通相结合,为流行病防范提供了实用价值。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查确定了 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 和人类 H1N2v 感染所暴露的通知能力方面的差距。虽然 监测 系统的建立是为了将动物、人类和环境健康联系起来,但该审查没有具体说明任何剩余的争议或未解决的机制,而是重点关注 进化 和综合方法的好处。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 这些影响凸显了在“同一个健康”框架下整合分子 流行病学、兽医现场监测、人工智能技术和跨部门沟通的实际价值。台湾的经验为其他国家克服猪流感 监测 碎片化和加强大流行防范提供了可复制的途径,强调了人类和动物卫生部门协调 监测 的重要性。

papers.title_zh: 猪流感进化和台湾的一次健康治理:从人畜共患病风险管理到综合防范。
papers.source_body_en: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) remain a persistent global threat because of rapid antigenic change, frequent genetic reassortment, and cross-species transmission. Swine act as key “mixing vessels,” permitting co-infection with avian and human strains and accelerating viral diversification and zoonotic risk. Effective veterinary surveillance is therefore critical for detecting viral evolution within swine populations and for providing early warning at the animal–human interface. Taiwan, home to approximately 5.5 million pigs and 23.4 million people, offers a representative case for examining how swine influenza surveillance has evolved in response to these challenges. This review describes the development of veterinary surveillance strategies from fragmented, event-driven monitoring to a coordinated One Health governance framework incorporating routine whole-genome sequencing, targeted serological surveillance, and coordinated data exchange across sectors. Key historical milestones include mass vaccination and culling programs, the 2009 pandemic response and recent zoonotic detections of H1N2v in humans (2021–2023), collectively evidencing ongoing bidirectional viral exchange. Episodes of severe human seasonal influenza activity, including H3N2-associated outbreaks, further highlighted the importance of coordinated surveillance across human and animal health sectors. By focusing on surveillance practices applied to animals, this review highlights the practical value of integrating molecular epidemiology, veterinary field monitoring, artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled technologies and cross-sector communication under a One Health framework. The Taiwanese experience demonstrates how strengthened veterinary surveillance can improve the sensitivity for detecting reassortment events, enhance traceability of viral spread, and support timely risk assessment in intensive livestock systems. These lessons offer a practical, replicable pathway for other countries aiming to overcome swine influenza surveillance fragmentation and strengthen pandemic preparedness under a One Health framework. The review traces Taiwan’s surveillance evolution from fragmented monitoring of swine influenza A viruses to a coordinated One Health governance model. A(H1N1)pdm09 and human H1N2v infections exposed gaps in notification capacity. The surveillance systems, genome sequencing and AI-enabled analytics are established to link animal, human, and environmental health for pandemic preparedness.

papers.title: A systematic meta-analytic comparative evaluation of seasonal influenza vaccine effectiveness from test-negative design studies in the Northern Hemisphere pre/post COVID-19 pandemic
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Influenza circulation was substantially reduced during the COVID-19 pandemic. The consequent reduction in population immunity may have resulted in increased influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) after the pandemic via reduced immunity in unvaccinated individuals compared to the pre-pandemic period. METHODS: We systematically reviewed published peer-reviewed test-negative design (TND) studies of seasonal influenza VE against medically-attended, laboratory-confirmed influenza in the Northern Hemisphere. We compared pooled VE estimates before (2010/11-2019/20) and after (2022/23-2024/25) the COVID-19 pandemic (defined as 2020/21-2021/22). Pooled VE against A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), influenza B, and B/Victoria was calculated for three age groups (6 months-17 years, 18-64 years, ≥65 years) using inverse-variance random-effects meta-analysis. Heterogeneity was quantified with the I2 statistic, and differences between pooled VE estimates pre- and post-pandemic periods were tested with the χ2 statistic. RESULTS: Eighty-five publications were included. Post-pandemic VE against A(H3N2) was significantly higher than pre-pandemic VE in 6-month-17-year-olds (53% [42-64%] vs 37% [30-45%]) and 18-64-year-olds (35% [25-45%] vs 21% [13-29%]). Similarly, VE against influenza B was higher post-pandemic in both age groups (85% [78-93%] vs 52% [45-60%] and 73% [59-87%] vs 49% [41-57%], respectively). Conversely, VE against A(H1N1)pdm09 was lower post-pandemic in 18-64-year-olds (37% [27-46%] vs 55% [47-62%]). No significant differences were observed for ≥65-year-olds, and data for B/Victoria were limited. CONCLUSIONS: The evidence suggests slightly higher VE against seasonal influenza after the COVID-19 pandemic although there may be factors other than population immunity that may explain our observations.

analysis_en.scope_and_question: This review evaluates seasonal influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) against A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), influenza B, and B/Victoria in the Northern Hemisphere, comparing pre- (2010/11-2019/20) and post- (2022/23-2024/25) COVID-19 pandemic periods across three age groups (6 months-17 years, 18-64 years, ≥65 years).
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic meta-analysis of 85 published test-negative design (TND) studies was conducted. Pooled VE estimates were calculated using inverse-variance random-effects meta-analysis, with heterogeneity quantified by I2 and statistical differences tested by χ2.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Post-pandemic VE against A(H3N2) and influenza B was significantly higher in 6-month-17-year-olds and 18-64-year-olds compared to pre-pandemic. Conversely, VE against A(H1N1)pdm09 was lower post-pandemic in 18-64-year-olds. No significant differences were observed for ≥65-year-olds, and B/Victoria data were limited.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The authors note that factors other than population immunity may explain the observed VE changes. Data for B/Victoria were limited, and no significant differences were found in the ≥65-year-old group, leaving gaps in understanding age-specific VE dynamics.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to explore factors beyond population immunity influencing post-pandemic VE, particularly in older adults and for B/Victoria. Surveillance should continue to monitor VE trends across age groups and virus subtypes.

papers.title_zh: 根据北半球 COVID-19 大流行前后测试阴性设计研究对 季节性流感 疫苗 有效性进行系统荟萃分析比较评估
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Influenza circulation was substantially reduced during the COVID-19 pandemic. The consequent reduction in population immunity may have resulted in increased influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) after the pandemic via reduced immunity in unvaccinated individuals compared to the pre-pandemic period. METHODS: We systematically reviewed published peer-reviewed test-negative design (TND) studies of seasonal influenza VE against medically-attended, laboratory-confirmed influenza in the Northern Hemisphere. We compared pooled VE estimates before (2010/11-2019/20) and after (2022/23-2024/25) the COVID-19 pandemic (defined as 2020/21-2021/22). Pooled VE against A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), influenza B, and B/Victoria was calculated for three age groups (6 months-17 years, 18-64 years, ≥65 years) using inverse-variance random-effects meta-analysis. Heterogeneity was quantified with the I2 statistic, and differences between pooled VE estimates pre- and post-pandemic periods were tested with the χ2 statistic. RESULTS: Eighty-five publications were included. Post-pandemic VE against A(H3N2) was significantly higher than pre-pandemic VE in 6-month-17-year-olds (53% [42-64%] vs 37% [30-45%]) and 18-64-year-olds (35% [25-45%] vs 21% [13-29%]). Similarly, VE against influenza B was higher post-pandemic in both age groups (85% [78-93%] vs 52% [45-60%] and 73% [59-87%] vs 49% [41-57%], respectively). Conversely, VE against A(H1N1)pdm09 was lower post-pandemic in 18-64-year-olds (37% [27-46%] vs 55% [47-62%]). No significant differences were observed for ≥65-year-olds, and data for B/Victoria were limited. CONCLUSIONS: The evidence suggests slightly higher VE against seasonal influenza after the COVID-19 pandemic although there may be factors other than population immunity that may explain our observations.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:在 COVID-19 大流行期间,流感传播大幅减少。与大流行前相比,由于未接种疫苗的个体免疫力下降,因此人群免疫力的降低可能导致大流行后流感 疫苗 有效性 (VE) 的增加。方法:我们系统地回顾了已发表的同行评审的 季节性流感 VE 对抗北半球经实验室确诊流感的同行评审试验阴性设计 (TND) 研究。我们比较了 COVID-19 大流行(定义为 2020/21-2021/22)之前(2010/11-2019/20)和之后(2022/23-2024/25)的汇总 VE 估计值。使用逆方差随机效应荟萃分析计算三个年龄组(6 个月至 17 岁、18-64 岁、≥65 岁)针对 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09、甲型H3N2流感病毒、乙型流感和 B/Victoria 的汇总 VE。使用 I2 统计量对异质性进行量化,并使用 χ2 统计量测试大流行前后的汇总 VE 估计值之间的差异。结果:纳入了 85 篇出版物。6 个月 17 岁儿童(53% [42-64%] vs 37% [30-45%])和 18-64 岁儿童(35% [25-45%] vs 21% [13-29%])中,针对 甲型H3N2流感病毒 的大流行后 VE 显着高于大流行前 VE。同样,两个年龄组的乙型流感 VE 在大流行后均较高(分别为 85% [78-93%] vs 52% [45-60%] 和 73% [59-87%] vs 49% [41-57%])。相反,大流行后 18-64 岁人群的 VE 相对于 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 较低(37% [27-46%] vs 55% [47-62%])。对于 65 岁以上的人群,没有观察到显着差异,并且 B/维多利亚的数据有限。结论:证据表明,在 COVID-19 大流行之后,针对 季节性流感 的 VE 略高,尽管除群体免疫力之外可能还有其他因素可以解释我们的观察结果。

papers.title: Epistasis facilitates the long-term antigenic evolution of the influenza B virus hemagglutinin
papers.abstract: The antigenic drift of viral glycoproteins must be balanced by purifying selection pressure to maintain functionality. Understanding these evolutionary processes is key to predicting and combating viral evolution but is primarily based on influenza A(H3N2), which may limit generalisability. By characterising the influenza B virus haemagglutinin (HA) over 8 decades of circulation in humans, we found continuous genetic diversification, punctuated with antigenic changes that did not follow a linear path in antigenic space. Antigenic change is primarily underpinned by re-occurring mutations and deletions at positions 136, 150, 162-165, 197 and 203. These residues form complex epistatic networks that modulate the antigenic impact of mutation recycling. They also generate permissive backbones on which immune escape can emerge with limited replicative fitness cost. Our study identifies critical similarities and differences with A(H3N2) evolution and demonstrates the role of epistasis in balancing antigenic novelty with viral fitness. Our findings and genetic, antigenic and phenotypic datasets support the development of genotype-to-phenotype prediction tools, but such predictions need to capture the complex outcomes of epistasis.

papers.title_zh: 上位性促进乙型流感病毒血凝素的长期抗原进化
papers.source_body_en: The antigenic drift of viral glycoproteins must be balanced by purifying selection pressure to maintain functionality. Understanding these evolutionary processes is key to predicting and combating viral evolution but is primarily based on influenza A(H3N2), which may limit generalisability. By characterising the influenza B virus haemagglutinin (HA) over 8 decades of circulation in humans, we found continuous genetic diversification, punctuated with antigenic changes that did not follow a linear path in antigenic space. Antigenic change is primarily underpinned by re-occurring mutations and deletions at positions 136, 150, 162-165, 197 and 203. These residues form complex epistatic networks that modulate the antigenic impact of mutation recycling. They also generate permissive backbones on which immune escape can emerge with limited replicative fitness cost. Our study identifies critical similarities and differences with A(H3N2) evolution and demonstrates the role of epistasis in balancing antigenic novelty with viral fitness. Our findings and genetic, antigenic and phenotypic datasets support the development of genotype-to-phenotype prediction tools, but such predictions need to capture the complex outcomes of epistasis.

papers.title: Effectiveness of seasonal influenza vaccine against dominant A(H1N1)pdm09 in adults ≥ 60 years: a multicenter test-negative design in Zhejiang, China, 2024–2025
papers.abstract: Zhejiang Province, China, has implemented a free influenza vaccination program for the elderly population for five consecutive years. However, data on real-world vaccine effectiveness against influenza among the local elderly population during the 2024–2025 influenza season are still lacking. A multicenter, retrospective test-negative design (TND) was adopted in this study. Sentinel surveillance networks were established across designated sentinel hospitals in six cities of Zhejiang Province, covering the period from October 2024 to July 2025. On a weekly basis, all or a systematic sample of patients aged ≥ 60 years presenting with influenza-like illness (ILI) were enrolled in the study. Epidemiological data were collected, respiratory specimens were obtained, and laboratory assays were conducted to detect influenza virus types and subtypes. Of the 4694 enrolled elderly patients with ILI, 1587 (33.81%) were influenza-positive, with A(H1N1)pdm09 being the dominant subtype (93.3%). Vaccination coverage was 32.72% (1536/4694). After adjusting for age, sex, chronic comorbidities, calendar week, and city, the overall VE was 53.3% (95% CI: 45.4–60.2). VE estimates by age group were 56.9% (95% CI: 45.8–65.8) for individuals aged 60–69 years, 51.2% (95% CI: 36.2–62.8) for 70–79 years, and 57.7% (95% CI: 37.2–71.8) for those aged ≥ 80 years. When compared with non-consecutive vaccination in the current season, VE for two, three, and four consecutive seasons was 44.6% (95% CI: 31.1–55.5), 35.5% (95% CI: 17.5–49.7), and 38.6% (95% CI: 18.8–53.6), respectively. Protection waned from 58.0% (95% CI: 37.6–71.7) within 59 days post-vaccination to 42.8% (95% CI: 33.4–50.9) between 60 and 180 days. Furthermore, vaccination provided effective protection against moderate-to-severe influenza (68.8%, 95% CI: 50.0-80.6) and influenza-associated hospitalization (53.9%, 95% CI: 37.3–66.0). In the 2024–2025 season in Zhejiang, influenza vaccination offered moderate protection against laboratory-confirmed influenza among adults aged ≥ 60 years. While VE waned over time, consecutive vaccination maintained moderate effectiveness. The vaccine also provided substantial protection against moderate-to-severe influenza and hospitalization.

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究对 季节性流感 疫苗 相对于 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 在老年人群中的有效性提供了基于证据的解释,强调了观察到的适度保护作用以及随着时间的推移有效性逐渐减弱。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为老年人群中流感 疫苗接种 的公共卫生策略提供信息,特别是关于 疫苗接种 的时间和频率,以保持对 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 的有效性。

papers.title: Identifying the viral and epidemiological factors behind the apparent global extinction of influenza B/Yamagata
papers.abstract: Until 2020, two lineages of the influenza B virus had co-circulated globally. Measures to control the COVID-19 pandemic led to a near-absence of influenza infections. While B/Victoria reemerged in late 2021, there have been no reports of B/Yamagata since the pandemic. To investigate which epidemiological and immunological factors were primarily responsible for the extinction of B/Yamagata, we developed a global model for the two influenza B lineages. To mimic the transmission impacts of the pandemic, we implemented a transient reduction in contacts and identified parameter values that recapitulated viral coexistence dynamic before the pandemic and the qualitative post-pandemic outcomes of B/Victoria (reemergence in late 2021) and B/Yamagata (extinction). Our results suggest that, rather than immunological or evolutionary mechanisms, the extinction of B/Yamagata was mainly driven by its lower basic reproduction number making the virus particularly vulnerable during the early phase of the pandemic. Stochastic simulations of our best-fitting model suggest that B/Victoria was also close to extinction during this period. We investigate the model to assess the feasibility of B/Victoria eradication through vaccination and the potential for a sustained re-emergence of B/Yamagata in the 2026-27 flu season, thus highlighting important considerations for biosafety. Significance For decades, the Yamagata and Victoria lineages of the influenza B virus co-circulated globally, causing millions of infections in humans. Only Victoria reemerged after the COVID-19 pandemic. By combining mechanistic transmission modeling with worldwide influenza surveillance data, we show that Yamagata’s extinction is most consistent with a lower intrinsic transmissibility than that of the surviving Victoria lineage. Contrary to other proposed explanations, differences in cross-immunity and immune escape appear insufficient to explain the observed outcome. Our analyses further indicate that Victoria narrowly avoided extinction during the COVID-19 disruption, but now transmission of Yamagata would be sustained if the lineage were reintroduced. These results inform both influenza eradication efforts and biosafety policy.

papers.abstract_zh: 直到 2020 年,两种乙型流感病毒谱系在全球范围内共同传播。控制 COVID-19 大流行的措施导致几乎没有流感感染。虽然 B/Victoria 于 2021 年底重新出现,但自大流行以来尚未有 B/Yamagata 的报告。为了调查哪些流行病学和免疫学因素是导致 B/Yamagata 灭绝的主要原因,我们开发了两个 B 型流感谱系的全球模型。为了模拟大流行的 传播 影响,我们暂时减少了接触,并确定了参数值,这些参数值概括了大流行之前的病毒共存动态以及 B/Victoria(于 2021 年底重新出现)和 B/Yamagata(灭绝)的大流行后定性结果。我们的结果表明,B/Yamagata 的灭绝主要是由于其较低的基本繁殖数,而不是免疫学或进化机制,使得该病毒在大流行的早期阶段特别脆弱。我们的最佳拟合模型的随机模拟表明,B/Victoria 在此期间也接近灭绝。我们研究了该模型,以评估通过 疫苗接种 根除 B/Victoria 的可行性以及 B/Yamagata 在 2026-27 流感季节持续重新出现的可能性,从而强调生物安全的重要考虑因素。意义 几十年来,乙型流感病毒的山形和维多利亚谱系在全球共同传播,导致数百万人感染。在 COVID-19 大流行之后,只有维多利亚重新出现。通过将机械 传播 模型与全球流感 监测 数据相结合,我们表明山形的灭绝与比幸存的维多利亚谱系更低的内在传播率最为一致。与其他提出的解释相反,交叉免疫和免疫逃逸的差异似乎不足以解释观察到的结果。我们的分析进一步表明,维多利亚在 COVID-19 破坏期间勉强避免了灭绝,但现在如果重新引入该谱系,山形的 传播 将得以维持。这些结果为根除流感工作和生物安全政策提供了信息。

papers.title: Epidemiological characteristics analysis of childhood influenza A virus infections in Hebei, China (2020–2024)
papers.abstract: Objective To analyze the epidemiological and infection characteristics of childhood influenza A virus infections in Hebei, China, from 2020 to 2024, and to provide a basis for influenza prevention and control among children. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on epidemiological and clinical data of children with influenza A virus infection who were hospitalized in Hebei Province from January 2020 to December 2024. Clinical specimens were analyzed using nucleic acid extraction reagents with automatic extraction on the Smart LabAssist-32 nucleic acid extractor. A 13-pathogen multiplex PCR detection kit combined with the GeXP multiplex gene expression analysis system was used for testing. Results A total of 298,810 specimens from children with upper and lower respiratory tract infections were collected. Among which 60,928 specimens were positive for influenza A virus (detection rate: 20.39%). The infection rate was highest in 2024 (23.03%) and lowest in 2020 (13.57%). The annual positive detection rates of influenza A virus in Hebei from 2020 to 2024 were 13.57%, 16.97%, 19.95%, 20.41%, and 23.03%, respectively, with statistically significant differences ( P < 0.05). The positive detection rate was significantly correlated with seasons, peaking in winter (29.04%) and reaching the lowest in spring and summer (5.4%). Mixed infections were detected in 16,049 specimens (26.34%), mainly involving rhinovirus, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP). Conclusion Pediatric influenza A virus infections in Hebei Province exhibit a clustered age distribution, pronounced seasonal variation, and a high co-infection rate. Enhanced surveillance and protective measures should be targeted toward children aged 1–5 years and prioritized during the winter season. This study provides important scientific evidence for optimizing influenza prevention and control strategies, clinical diagnosis, and treatment.

papers.title: Flu Mutation Explorer: an Interactive Platform for Mapping Host Adaptation Mutations in Influenza A Viruses
papers.abstract: Abstract A rapid expansion of influenza A virus (IAV) genome sequencing has transformed global surveillance but has also created major challenges for interpreting the biological significance of viral mutations, particularly amino acid replacements associated with host adaptation. Resources have been created to support mutation annotation and phylogenetic analysis, but there is a need for a tool that integrates experimentally derived phenotypic evidence with evolutionary context in a framework suitable for users without prior training in bioinformatics. Here, we present the Flu Mutation Explorer, an interactive web application that combines large-scale influenza phylogenies with a manually curated database of reported mammalian adaptation mutations, to enable the exploration and interpretation of IAV genetic variation. The underlying database comprises over 1.5 million publicly available IAV sequences and over 1000 mutations associated with mammalian adaptation. The Flu Mutation Explorer enables users to query protein sequences, visualise amino acid distributions across viral lineages, examine host-specific conservation patterns, and identify adaptation mutation with links to supporting literature. We include case studies which demonstrate the platform’s use in assessing amino acid conservation at sites of interest and in rapidly identifying candidate mammalian adaptation mutations during the ongoing H5N1 panzootic. By integrating genomic, phylogenetic, and functional information into an intuitive interface, the Flu Mutation Explorer lowers the barriers to interpreting influenza sequences for specialists and non-specialists alike.

papers.source_body_en: Abstract A rapid expansion of influenza A virus (IAV) genome sequencing has transformed global surveillance but has also created major challenges for interpreting the biological significance of viral mutations, particularly amino acid replacements associated with host adaptation. Resources have been created to support mutation annotation and phylogenetic analysis, but there is a need for a tool that integrates experimentally derived phenotypic evidence with evolutionary context in a framework suitable for users without prior training in bioinformatics. Here, we present the Flu Mutation Explorer, an interactive web application that combines large-scale influenza phylogenies with a manually curated database of reported mammalian adaptation mutations, to enable the exploration and interpretation of IAV genetic variation. The underlying database comprises over 1.5 million publicly available IAV sequences and over 1000 mutations associated with mammalian adaptation. The Flu Mutation Explorer enables users to query protein sequences, visualise amino acid distributions across viral lineages, examine host-specific conservation patterns, and identify adaptation mutation with links to supporting literature. We include case studies which demonstrate the platform’s use in assessing amino acid conservation at sites of interest and in rapidly identifying candidate mammalian adaptation mutations during the ongoing H5N1 panzootic. By integrating genomic, phylogenetic, and functional information into an intuitive interface, the Flu Mutation Explorer lowers the barriers to interpreting influenza sequences for specialists and non-specialists alike.

papers.title: Risk Factors for Mortality Associated With Influenza Infection in Patients With Hematologic Malignancies: A Cross‐Sectional Descriptive Observational Study
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aims Cancer patients, especially those with hematologic malignancies (HMs), are considered among the most vulnerable groups at risk for severe outcomes from influenza infection. This study aimed to investigate influenza infection in patients with HMs and identify the risk factors associated with mortality. Methods This cross‐sectional descriptive observational study included 90 patients with confirmed influenza infection and HMs. The data collected included demographic information, cancer type and status, influenza type, symptoms, laboratory and radiologic findings, length of hospital stay, ICU admissions, and mortality rate. The primary outcome was analysis endpoints included mortality risk factors based on ICU admission, death and type of malignancies. Results The mean age of patients was 34.3 ± 26.7 years (median 34, range 2–91). Most had acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL, 45.6%), followed by acute myeloid leukemia (AML, 22.2%), lymphomas (14.4%), multiple myeloma (MM, 6.7%), chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML, 2.2%), and other malignancies (8.9%). Nearly half (49.3%) were in the maintenance phase of treatment, and 80% were infected with influenza A. Pleural effusion (22.2%) and ground‐glass opacities (17.8%) were the most common radiologic findings. ICU admission was significantly linked to older age ( p = 0.002), comorbidity ( p = 0.003), lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) ( p = 0.02), muscle ache ( p = 0.03), and malignancies including MM, CML, and AML ( p = 0.02). Higher mortality was observed in patients with MM or AML ( p = 0.01), comorbidities ( p = 0.02), and LRTIs ( p = 0.04). Age‐adjusted analysis confirmed MM, LRTI, and comorbidity as potential strong predictors of mortality. Conclusion ICU admission was significantly associated with older age, the presence of at least one comorbidity, LRTI, and body muscle aches. MM, CML, and AML were notably more associated with ICU admission. Patients diagnosed with MM and AML, those with at least one comorbidity, and those with LRTIs had a higher risk of mortality. The age‐adjusted analysis identified MM, LRTIs, and comorbidities as potential strong predictors of mortality in this cohort, requiring validation in larger studies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the antiviral effects of Artemisia extracts against seasonal influenza viruses, particularly highlighting the need to explore natural compounds for combating influenza infections due to their potential to target viral proteins and modulate host immune responses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in a laboratory setting using in vitro models to evaluate the effects of Artemisia extracts on seasonal influenza viruses, including H1N1pdm09 and H3N2, with a focus on their interaction with viral HA/NA proteins and the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling pathway.
analysis.methods: The researchers used cell culture assays to assess the antiviral activity of Artemisia extracts, including measuring viral replication inhibition and evaluating the modulation of the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling pathway through molecular and biochemical techniques.
analysis.main_results: Artemisia extracts significantly suppressed H1N1pdm09 and H3N2 viral replication, with a 70% reduction in viral titers observed in infected cells, and demonstrated a notable modulation of the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling pathway.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that Artemisia extracts may offer a novel therapeutic approach by targeting viral proteins and influencing host immune responses, providing a potential alternative to conventional antiviral treatments.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results could inform the development of new antiviral therapies and contribute to the understanding of natural compounds' roles in combating seasonal influenza, potentially supporting further research into plant-based treatments.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro models, which may not fully reflect in vivo conditions, and the evidence is moderate due to the lack of clinical trials or long-term efficacy data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在研究艾蒿提取物对 季节性流感 病毒的 抗病毒药物 作用,特别强调需要探索天然化合物来对抗流感感染,因为它们具有靶向病毒蛋白和调节 宿主 免疫应答 的潜力。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是在实验室环境中使用体外模型评估艾蒿提取物对 季节性流感 病毒(包括 H1N1pdm09 和 H3N2)的影响,重点是它们与病毒 HA/NA 蛋白和 TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB 信号通路的相互作用。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用细胞培养测定来评估蒿提取物的 抗病毒药物 活性,包括测量病毒复制抑制并通过分子和生化技术评估 TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB 信号通路的调节。
elements_zh.main_results: 蒿提取物显着抑制 H1N1pdm09 和 H3N2 病毒复制,在感染细胞中观察到病毒滴度降低 70%,并显示出对 TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB 信号通路的显着调节。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,艾蒿提取物可能通过靶向病毒蛋白并影响 宿主 免疫应答 来提供一种新的治疗方法,为传统 抗病毒药物 治疗 提供潜在的替代品。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果可以为新 抗病毒药物 疗法的开发提供信息,并有助于了解天然化合物在对抗 季节性流感 中的作用,从而有可能支持对基于植物的 治疗 的进一步研究。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于体外模型,可能无法完全反映体内情况,且由于缺乏临床试验或长期疗效数据,证据不充分。

papers.title: LncRNA ckATP1A1-AS1 inhibits influenza A virus replication by mediating innate immune responses and suppressing viral nuclear import
papers.abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) pose an ongoing threat to humans and other species because of their zoonotic potential. Accumulating evidence has demonstrated that certain long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) exhibit differential expression during viral infection and modulate diverse facets of viral pathogenesis. As key regulatory RNAs, lncRNAs participate in fundamental physiological processes and disease progression via a wide array of functional interactions with DNA, RNA, and proteins. Here, we identified ckATP1A1-AS1 as an antiviral host lncRNA that is induced by IAV infection. Functional analyses demonstrated that ckATP1A1-AS1 overexpression restricted infection by multiple IAV subtypes, whereas ckATP1A1-AS1 knockdown enhanced viral replication. Mechanistically, during IAV infection, the transcription factor JUN transcriptionally activates ckATP1A1-AS1, which further enhances the expression of interferon-β and key interferon-stimulated genes, thereby positively regulating type I interferon immune responses. Furthermore, ckATP1A1-AS1 interacts directly with the viral nucleoprotein, competitively disrupting its binding to importin α5, impairing its oligomerization, and blocking the nuclear import of viral ribonucleoprotein complexes. Consequently, ckATP1A1-AS1 suppresses viral ribonucleoprotein assembly and reduces viral polymerase activity. These findings establish ckATP1A1-AS1 as a key antiviral lncRNA that restricts IAV replication by coordinating innate immune signaling and directly targeting several steps in the viral replication cycle. IMPORTANCE: Accumulating evidence indicates that host long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play important roles in regulating virus-host interactions during influenza A virus (IAV) infection. However, the functions and mechanisms of action of most IAV-associated lncRNAs remain unclear. This study identifies the novel chicken antisense lncRNA ckATP1A1-AS1 as a key antiviral factor with a unique dual mechanism: it is transcriptionally activated by transcription factor JUN and, in turn, upregulates the expression of interferon-β and key interferon-stimulated genes to positively regulate the type I interferon immune response. It directly interacts with viral nucleoprotein, competitively disrupting the binding of nucleoprotein to importin α5 and impairing nucleoprotein oligomerization, thereby suppressing viral ribonucleoprotein assembly and reducing viral polymerase activity.

Consequently, ckATP1A1-AS1 suppresses viral ribonucleoprotein assembly and reduces viral polymerase activity. These findings establish ckATP1A1-AS1 as a key antiviral lncRNA that restricts IAV replication by coordinating innate immune signaling and directly targeting several steps in the viral replication cycle. IMPORTANCE: Accumulating evidence indicates that host long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play important roles in regulating virus-host interactions during influenza A virus (IAV) infection. However, the functions and mechanisms of action of most IAV-associated lncRNAs remain unclear. This study identifies the novel chicken antisense lncRNA ckATP1A1-AS1 as a key antiviral factor with a unique dual mechanism: it is transcriptionally activated by transcription factor JUN and, in turn, upregulates the expression of interferon-β and key interferon-stimulated genes to positively regulate the type I interferon immune response. papers.title: A chicken interferon stimulated gene screen reveals limited genes restricting influenza replication
papers.abstract: Avian influenza A virus (IAV) is a major global health threat. Not only does it cause significant economic losses to the agricultural industry, but it also presents a risk of spillover into the human population. However, several obstacles must be overcome for a successful cross-species transmission event to occur. One of these obstacles is the innate immunity of the host. While the innate immune response to IAV in humans has been well-studied, the innate immune response to IAV in birds is not as well understood. Here, we explore the interferon-induced immune response by identifying interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) in chicken, quail, and duck cells, and find that they are largely species-specific. Using this data, we performed a CRISPR knockout ISG screen against two strains of IAV, the mouse-adapted PR8, and the low pathogenicity avian IAV isolate WF10. We find that for PR8, IFITM3 is the dominant restrictor of viral replication with several additional hits with modest effects, consistent with previous work in mammals. For avian WF10, IFITM3 was also a hit however there were two additional hits absent for PR8, the HSP70 co-chaperone protein BAG5 and deubiquitinase OTUD4. Overall, these findings confirm the divergence of interferon-mediated immunity between species and establish a screening system that can be used to identify ISGs important for viral restriction in avian species.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Avian influenza A virus (IAV) poses a significant global health threat, causing economic losses and risking spillover into humans, but the innate immune response to IAV in birds is not well understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study performed a CRISPR knockout interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) screen in chicken, quail, and duck cells against two strains of IAV: the mouse-adapted PR8 and the low pathogenicity avian IAV isolate WF10.
analysis.methods: Using CRISPR knockout technology, the researchers identified ISGs in avian cells and screened them against two IAV strains to determine which genes restrict viral replication.
analysis.main_results: For PR8, IFITM3 was the dominant restrictor of viral replication with several additional hits having modest effects; for avian WF10, IFITM3 was also a hit, but two additional hits, BAG5 and OTUD4, were absent for PR8.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings confirm the divergence of interferon-mediated immunity between species and establish a screening system to identify ISGs important for viral restriction in avian species.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides insights into species-specific immune responses to IAV, which can inform surveillance and control strategies for avian influenza and potential zoonotic transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, as the study focuses on avian species and specific IAV strains, limiting generalizability to human seasonal influenza viruses.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the innate immune response to avian influenza A virus (IAV) by identifying interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) in chicken, quail, and duck cells. Using a CRISPR knockout screen against two IAV strains (PR8 and WF10), the researchers found that IFITM3 is the dominant restrictor of viral replication for PR8, while WF10 additionally involves BAG5 and OTUD4. The findings highlight species-specific differences in interferon-mediated immunity and establish a screening system for identifying ISGs in avian species, with moderate evidence strength due to the focus on avian models.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 甲型禽流感病毒 (IAV) 对全球健康构成重大威胁,造成经济损失,并给人类带来 跨物种溢出 的风险,但鸟类对 IAV 的先天 免疫应答 尚不清楚。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究在鸡、鹌鹑和鸭细胞中针对两种 IAV 株进行了 CRISPR 敲除干扰素刺激基因 (ISG) 筛选:小鼠适应性 PR8 和低致病性禽 IAV 分离株 WF10。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员利用 CRISPR 敲除技术,在禽类细胞中鉴定了 ISG,并对两种 IAV 毒株进行筛选,以确定哪些基因限制病毒复制。

papers.title_zh: 鸡干扰素刺激基因筛选揭示限制流感复制的有限基因
papers.source_body_en: Avian influenza A virus (IAV) is a major global health threat. Not only does it cause significant economic losses to the agricultural industry, but it also presents a risk of spillover into the human population. However, several obstacles must be overcome for a successful cross-species transmission event to occur. One of these obstacles is the innate immunity of the host. While the innate immune response to IAV in humans has been well-studied, the innate immune response to IAV in birds is not as well understood. Here, we explore the interferon-induced immune response by identifying interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) in chicken, quail, and duck cells, and find that they are largely species-specific. Using this data, we performed a CRISPR knockout ISG screen against two strains of IAV, the mouse-adapted PR8, and the low pathogenicity avian IAV isolate WF10. We find that for PR8, IFITM3 is the dominant restrictor of viral replication with several additional hits with modest effects, consistent with previous work in mammals. For avian WF10, IFITM3 was also a hit however there were two additional hits absent for PR8, the HSP70 co-chaperone protein BAG5 and deubiquitinase OTUD4. Overall, these findings confirm the divergence of interferon-mediated immunity between species and establish a screening system that can be used to identify ISGs important for viral restriction in avian species.

papers.title: H5N1 influenza binding and cell entry via human class II MHC, and blocking by cross-reactive antibodies
papers.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses are currently responsible for a multi-species outbreak affecting wild birds, poultry, numerous mammalian species, and humans. Influenza A viruses typically initiate infection through binding to sialic acid, although select bat and human influenza viruses can also exploit class II major histocompatibility complex (MHC-II) molecules for cell entry. Here we show that emerging H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses, but not historical H5 lineages, bind human MHC-II HLA-DR and mediate sialic acid-independent cell entry. Hemagglutinin binding to primary human immune cells varies with MHC-II expression and is further shaped by HLA-DR allelic variation, identifying host genetic determinants that may influence susceptibility to infection. Mammalian-adaptive substitutions within the hemagglutinin sialic acid receptor-binding domain reduce MHC-II binding, suggesting this interaction is remodeled during clade 2.3.4.4b H5 adaptation to a human host. Lastly, cross-reactive monoclonal antibodies isolated from clade 2.3.4.4b H5-naive humans can block the hemagglutinin-MHC-II interaction. These findings identify a previously unrecognized receptor pathway in contemporary H5N1 viruses and reveal that both human genetic variation and pre-existing humoral immunity can modulate this interaction, with implications for host range, cellular tropism, spillover risk, and therapeutic intervention.

papers.abstract_zh: 高致病性禽流感 H5N1 分支 2.3.4.4b 病毒目前导致多物种 暴发 影响野生鸟类、家禽、众多哺乳动物物种和人类。甲型流感病毒通常通过与唾液酸结合来启动感染,尽管某些蝙蝠和人类流感病毒也可以利用 II 类主要组织相容性复合物 (MHC-II) 分子进入细胞。在这里,我们表明新兴的 H5N1 分支 2.3.4.4b 病毒(而不是历史的 H5 谱系)结合人类 MHC-II HLA-DR 并介导不依赖唾液酸的细胞进入。血凝素与初级人类免疫细胞的结合随 MHC-II 表达的变化而变化,并进一步受到 HLA-DR 等位基因变异的影响,从而识别出可能影响感染易感性的 宿主 遗传决定因素。血凝素唾液酸受体结合域内的哺乳动物适应性取代减少了 MHC-II 结合,表明这种相互作用在进化枝 2.3.4.4b H5 适应人类 宿主 过程中被重塑。最后,从进化枝 2.3.4.4b H5 未接触过的人中分离出的交叉反应单克隆抗体可以阻断血凝素-MHC-II 相互作用。这些发现确定了当代 H5N1 病毒中以前未被识别的受体途径,并揭示人类遗传变异和预先存在的体液免疫可以调节这种相互作用,对 宿主 范围、细胞向性、跨物种溢出 风险和治疗干预具有影响。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现揭示了当代 H5N1 病毒中以前未被识别的受体途径,强调了 宿主 遗传变异和预先存在的免疫力在调节病毒进入中的作用。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果对于了解 H5N1 病毒的 宿主 范围、细胞向性和 跨物种溢出 风险具有重要意义,可能为 监测、诊断 和治疗策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅基于抽象证据,这可能会限制分析的深度,但研究结果得到了对病毒结合和遗传适应的直接观察的支持。

papers.title: From neuraminidase inhibitors to novel mechanisms: expanding therapeutic strategies against influenza
papers.abstract: Seasonal influenza causes approximately one billion infections and up to 650,000 respiratory deaths annually. Despite decades of antiviral development, the therapeutic arsenal remains constrained by time-dependent efficacy (clinical benefit confined largely to treatment initiated within 48 hours of symptom onset), low genetic resistance barriers (resistance arising from a single point mutation), and critical evidence gaps in high-risk populations. This review critically evaluates the antiviral landscape, focusing on next-generation cap-dependent endonuclease inhibitors (CENIs), resistance implications across all approved drug classes, translational barriers in host-directed therapies and biologics, and H5N1 pandemic preparedness. Suraxavir marboxil, ZX-7101A, and the first approved polymerase basic protein 2 (PB2) inhibitor, onradivir, confirm that scaffold-level optimization (incremental structural refinement within an existing drug class) can meaningfully reduce resistance emergence rates. Across all approved classes, a shared failure pattern is evident: single-target dependence, low-fitness-cost resistance mutations (mutations that confer drug resistance without measurably impairing viral replication or transmission), and a therapeutic window that most patients do not reach. Combination antiviral therapy shows promise for resistance prevention, though the FLAGSTONE Phase 3 trial demonstrated that virological benefit does not consistently translate to clinical outcomes in hospitalized patients. Host-directed therapies and biologics face a shared translational obstacle: the biological window of maximal activity consistently precedes the clinical window of patient presentation, and systemic biologics cannot achieve inhibitory concentrations at the respiratory mucosal surface. For H5N1, preparedness relies on a single observationally supported drug class; baloxavir is absent from most national stockpiles, and no randomized trial data exists for any antiviral in human H5N1 infection. Adaptive trial infrastructure, diversified stockpiling to include next-generation CENIs, and equitable global antiviral access are the most urgent priorities in influenza therapeutics.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates therapeutic strategies against seasonal influenza, highlighting limitations of current antivirals, including time-dependent efficacy, low resistance barriers, and evidence gaps in high-risk populations. elements_zh.scope_and_question: 季节性流感 病毒(甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09、甲型H3N2流感病毒、B/Victoria 和历史 B/Yamagata)每年造成约 10 亿感染和多达 650,000 例呼吸道死亡。核心问题是如何扩展治疗策略以超越当前的限制。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述严格评估了 抗病毒药物 的前景,重点关注下一代帽依赖性核酸内切酶抑制剂 (CENI)、所有已批准药物类别的耐药性影响、宿主 导向疗法和生物制剂的转化障碍,以及 H5N1 大流行的防范。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 支架级优化(例如 Suraxavir marboxil、ZX-7101A、onradivir)可以降低耐药性出现率。然而,所有批准的类别都有一个失败模式:单靶点依赖性、低适应成本耐药性 突变 以及大多数患者无法达到的治疗窗口。联合治疗显示出预防耐药性的希望,但病毒学益处并不能始终转化为住院患者的临床结果。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 宿主定向疗法和生物制剂面临转化障碍:它们的生物活性窗口先于临床表现,并且全身生物制剂无法在呼吸道粘膜表面达到抑制浓度。对于 H5N1,准备工作依赖于单一的观察支持的药物类别;大多数库存中不存在巴洛沙韦,并且没有针对人类 H5N1 感染的任何 抗病毒药物 的随机试验数据。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 适应性试验基础设施、包括下一代 CENI 在内的多元化库存以及公平的全球 抗病毒药物 获取是流感治疗中最紧迫的优先事项。

papers.title: Pandemic Influenza Protection Before Day One: Modeling the Impact of a Broadly Cross-Reactive Seasonal Vaccine
papers.abstract: Abstract Pandemic influenza poses a constant threat to domestic and global public health with the potential of high morbidity and mortality. Pandemic virus-matched vaccines, though potentially highly efficacious, require a lead time before they can be mass-produced and distributed to the population. For this reason, mitigation strategies that provide protection ahead of widespread viral transmission are highly desirable. Here, we model the impact of a broadly cross-reactive seasonal influenza vaccine on pandemic influenza spread in the U.S. Our findings indicate that as the cross-protective efficacy of the seasonal vaccine against the pandemic variant increases, total hospitalizations are concomitantly reduced. For example, we find that even at typical seasonal vaccine uptake and modest vaccine efficacies against infection and hospitalization with the pandemic variant, total hospitalizations can be decreased by 30% or more across the scenarios considered. In addition, the hospitalization risk for recipients is at least 35% lower than the risk experienced by unvaccinated persons. These results demonstrate that a broadly protective influenza vaccine could serve as a critical component of pandemic preparedness strategies.

Pandemic virus-matched vaccines, though potentially highly efficacious, require a lead time before they can be mass-produced and distributed to the population. For this reason, mitigation strategies that provide protection ahead of widespread viral transmission are highly desirable. Here, we model the impact of a broadly cross-reactive seasonal influenza vaccine on pandemic influenza spread in the U.S. Our findings indicate that as the cross-protective efficacy of the seasonal vaccine against the pandemic variant increases, total hospitalizations are concomitantly reduced. For example, we find that even at typical seasonal vaccine uptake and modest vaccine efficacies against infection and hospitalization with the pandemic variant, total hospitalizations can be decreased by 30% or more across the scenarios considered. In addition, the hospitalization risk for recipients is at least 35% lower than the risk experienced by unvaccinated persons. These results demonstrate that a broadly protective influenza vaccine could serve as a critical component of pandemic preparedness strategies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Pandemic influenza poses a constant threat to domestic and global public health with the potential of high morbidity and mortality. The study aimed to evaluate the potential of a broadly cross-reactive seasonal influenza vaccine to mitigate pandemic influenza spread.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a modeling analysis of pandemic influenza spread in the U.S., focusing on the impact of a broadly cross-reactive seasonal influenza vaccine. It considers various scenarios of vaccine uptake and efficacy against the pandemic variant.
analysis.methods: The research employed mathematical modeling to simulate the impact of a seasonal influenza vaccine with cross-reactive properties on pandemic influenza spread. The model incorporated typical seasonal vaccine uptake rates and assumed modest vaccine efficacies against infection and hospitalization with the pandemic variant.
analysis.main_results: The findings indicate that as the cross-protective efficacy of the seasonal vaccine against the pandemic variant increases, total hospitalizations are concomitantly reduced. For example, even at typical seasonal vaccine uptake and modest vaccine efficacies, total hospitalizations can be decreased by 30% or more across the scenarios considered.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that a broadly protective influenza vaccine could serve as a critical component of pandemic preparedness strategies. This is a novel approach to pandemic mitigation by leveraging existing seasonal vaccine infrastructure.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that seasonal influenza vaccines with cross-reactive properties could have significant implications for pandemic preparedness, offering a potential tool to reduce hospitalizations and mitigate the impact of future outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on modeling and does not involve empirical data, which limits the strength of the evidence. However, the findings are grounded in plausible assumptions about vaccine efficacy and uptake, supporting a moderate confidence level.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the potential of a broadly cross-reactive seasonal influenza vaccine to reduce the impact of pandemic influenza in the U.S. The research is based on mathematical modeling that simulates various scenarios of vaccine uptake and efficacy against pandemic variants. The findings suggest that even modest cross-protective effects could lead to a significant reduction in hospitalizations. The authors interpret these results as demonstrating the value of seasonal vaccines in pandemic preparedness. The study highlights the importance of cross-reactive vaccines in mitigating the spread of pandemic influenza, but its reliance on modeling limits the strength of the evidence. The implications of this research could inform future strategies for pandemic mitigation by leveraging existing seasonal vaccine programs.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是对美国大流行性流感传播的建模分析,重点关注广泛交叉反应的 季节性流感 疫苗 的影响。它考虑了 疫苗 的吸收和针对大流行变体的功效的各种情况。

elements_zh.main_results: 研究结果表明,随着季节性 疫苗 针对大流行变异的交叉保护功效增加,住院总人数也随之减少。例如,即使在典型的季节性 疫苗 吸收和适度的 疫苗 功效下,在考虑的场景中,总住院率也可以减少 30% 或更多。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,具有广泛保护性的流感 疫苗 可以作为大流行防范策略的关键组成部分。这是一种利用现有季节性 疫苗 基础设施来缓解流行病的新颖方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果表明,具有交叉反应特性的 季节性流感 疫苗 可能对大流行的防范产生重大影响,为减少住院治疗和减轻未来 暴发 的影响提供了潜在的工具。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于模型,不涉及经验数据,这限制了证据的强度。然而,研究结果基于有关 疫苗 功效和吸收的合理假设,支持适度的置信水平。

papers.title: SNHG15 Positively Regulates Influenza Virus Infection Through Its Association With miR-153 and RABL2A.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Influenza viruses cause seasonal epidemics, and current vaccines do not fully protect against them. This study focuses on long non‐coding RNAs (lncRNAs), which are RNA molecules that do not code for proteins but play crucial roles in various biological processes. We identified 17 lncRNAs altered by the influenza virus. Among these, SNHG15 was found to enhance influenza virus infection. Knockdown of SNHG15 using CRISPR interference and RNA interference reduced influenza virus infection, while overexpression of SNHG15 increased virus replication. We found that miR‐153‐3p, a competitive endogenous RNA (ceRNA) for SNHG15, acts as an anti‐influenza microRNA, and its overexpression negated SNHG15's proviral activity. RNA pull‐down and mass spectrometry identified Rab‐like protein 2A (RABL2A) as an interacting partner of SNHG15. Both SNHG15 and RABL2A facilitated influenza virus internalization. Additionally, siRNA‐mediated knockdown of RABL2A reduced SNHG15‐mediated virus internalization. In conclusion, SNHG15 enhances influenza A virus infection through its interactions with miR‐153 and RABL2A.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in influenza virus infection, identifying SNHG15 as a key enhancer. papers.title_zh: SNHG15 通过与 miR-153 和 RABL2A 的关联积极调节流感病毒感染。
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Influenza viruses cause seasonal epidemics, and current vaccines do not fully protect against them. This study focuses on long non‐coding RNAs (lncRNAs), which are RNA molecules that do not code for proteins but play crucial roles in various biological processes. We identified 17 lncRNAs altered by the influenza virus. Among these, SNHG15 was found to enhance influenza virus infection. Knockdown of SNHG15 using CRISPR interference and RNA interference reduced influenza virus infection, while overexpression of SNHG15 increased virus replication. We found that miR‐153‐3p, a competitive endogenous RNA (ceRNA) for SNHG15, acts as an anti‐influenza microRNA, and its overexpression negated SNHG15's proviral activity. RNA pull‐down and mass spectrometry identified Rab‐like protein 2A (RABL2A) as an interacting partner of SNHG15. Both SNHG15 and RABL2A facilitated influenza virus internalization. Additionally, siRNA‐mediated knockdown of RABL2A reduced SNHG15‐mediated virus internalization. In conclusion, SNHG15 enhances influenza A virus infection through its interactions with miR‐153 and RABL2A.

papers.title: Assessment of Timing for Influenza Vaccination among Older Adults in Japan: The VENUS Study.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: In Japan, seasonal influenza vaccination is recommended for older adults between October and mid-December; however, the optimal vaccination timing remains unclear owing to waning immunity and variable epidemic patterns. In this study, we aimed to assess the effectiveness of different vaccination strategies in reducing influenza-related outcomes in older adults. METHODS: Using data from the VENUS Study, we conducted a target trial emulation including adults aged ≥65 years across four influenza seasons (2016/2017, 2017/2018, 2018/2019, and 2019/2020). We applied a cloning, censoring, and weighting approach. Each individual was cloned and assigned to one of seven vaccination strategies at the start of October: no vaccination, vaccination during October, October-November, October-December, November, November-December, or December. Outcomes included influenza, influenza-related hospitalization, and all-cause mortality. Risk ratios (RRs) and risk differences (RDs), relative to no vaccination, were estimated at the end of March for each season based on standardized cumulative incidence. RESULTS: Annual cohorts included 131,178-138,438 individuals (median age: 76-78 years; male sex: 40.1-41.0%). The influenza incidences and RRs varied by season. Delayed vaccination was associated with the lowest influenza incidence in 2017/2018 and 2018/2019, but not in the other seasons. Influenza-related hospitalizations showed seasonal trends similar to those of influenza. In contrast, early vaccination strategies generally led to reduced all-cause mortality across all seasons. The RRs were 0.80-0.93, 0.80-0.95, 0.82-1.00, and 0.81-0.96 in the 2016/2017, 2017/2018, 2018/2019, and 2019/2020 seasons, respectively. The RDs were larger for mortality than for the influenza-related outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: The effectiveness of each timing strategy varied depending on the outcome and season. Although delayed vaccination was associated with a lower influenza incidence in some seasons, early vaccination generally reduced all-cause mortality.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 在日本,建议老年人在 10 月至 12 月中旬期间服用 季节性流感 疫苗接种;然而,由于免疫力下降和流行模式多变,疫苗接种 的最佳时机仍不清楚。在本研究中,我们旨在评估不同 疫苗接种 策略在减少老年人流感相关结果方面的有效性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 利用 VENUS 研究的数据,我们进行了一项目标试验模拟,包括四个流感季节(2016/2017、2017/2018、2018/2019 和 2019/2020)年龄≥65 岁的成年人。结果包括流感、流感相关住院治疗和全因 死亡率。
elements_zh.methods: 我们应用了克隆、审查和加权方法。每个人在 10 月初都被克隆并分配到七个 疫苗接种 策略之一:10 月期间无 疫苗接种、疫苗接种、10 月至 11 月、10 月至 12 月、11 月、11 月至 12 月或 12 月。相对于无 发病率 的风险比 (RR) 和风险差 (RD) 在每个季节的 3 月底根据标准化累积 发病率 进行估计。
elements_zh.main_results: 年度 队列研究 包括 131,178-138,438 人(中位年龄:76-78 岁;男性:40.1-41.0%)。流感 发病率 和 RR 随季节变化。延迟的 疫苗接种 与 2017/2018 和 2018/2019 年流感 发病率 最低水平相关,但与其他季节无关。与流感相关的住院治疗表现出与流感相似的季节性趋势。相比之下,早期的 疫苗接种 策略通常会导致所有季节的全因 死亡率 减少。2016/2017、2017/2018、2018/2019和2019/2020赛季的RR分别为0.80-0.93、0.80-0.95、0.82-1.00和0.81-0.96。死亡率 的 RD 大于流感相关结果的 RD。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 每种计时策略的有效性取决于结果和季节。虽然延迟的 疫苗接种 在某些季节与较低的流感 发病率 相关,但早期的 疫苗接种 通常会减少全因 发病率。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,疫苗接种 的时机应根据季节和结果进行调整,尽管对流感 发病率 的影响各不相同,但早期的 疫苗接种 可能会减少 死亡率。这可以为优化老年人流感 疫苗接种 策略的公共卫生建议提供参考。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究使用目标试验模拟,这可能会引入观察数据固有的局限性。然而,大样本量和跨多个季节的一致结果为研究结果提供了适度的信心。

papers.title: Enhancing knowledge on influenza and other pandemic threats for healthcare personnel readiness in Thailand, 2007–2024
papers.abstract: Healthcare personnel are often the first line of defense against emerging diseases. Enhancing knowledge on influenza for healthcare personnel is part of Thailand’s influenza pandemic preparedness plan. Beginning in 2007, the Thailand Department of Medical Services organized trainings for Thai healthcare personnel in Bangkok and all regions of Thailand on prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and control of human seasonal, avian, and pandemic influenza. The curriculum included overviews on the global situation, clinical features and treatment, influenza epidemiology and burden in Thailand, influenza as a cause of pneumonia, laboratory diagnostics, impact of influenza in high-risk populations and increased risk for complications; influenza economic evaluation of seasonal influenza vaccination in Thailand, and immunization and planning for human influenza outbreaks. Topics initially focused on seasonal and pandemic influenza and expanded in scope to incorporate other pandemic threats, such as MERS-CoV and COVID-19. From August 2007 through December 2024, 114 trainings were conducted. A total of 26,422 attendees (range 10–700 per training) were trained, including clinicians, nurses, pharmacists, laboratory technicians, and public health scientists (professionals trained in epidemiology, disease surveillance, and health data analysis) from public and private hospitals from national, regional, provincial, and district levels in Bangkok and 41 provinces nationwide. During training sessions, participants reported that the program increased their readiness and self-reported confidence to respond to potential respiratory outbreaks. These capacity-building efforts contributed to a health workforce that was better positioned to respond to emerging respiratory threats, including the first wave of COVID-19. Educating healthcare personnel about prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and control of influenza is an important component of pandemic preparedness. Refresher courses or online tutorials may be needed periodically to maintain current knowledge.

papers.title: Parameterization of the PA Endonuclease Bimetallic Center Reveals the Dynamics of Clinically Relevant Mutations.
papers.abstract: Influenza A virus continues to impose a major global health and economic burden through seasonal epidemics and occasional pandemics, highlighting the critical need for continued antiviral development. As the latest addition to anti-influenza therapy, baloxavir marboxil (BXM) targets the highly conserved PA N-terminal endonuclease domain (PAN), blocking the cap-snatching process essential for viral transcription initiation. However, the rapid emergence of resistance mutations significantly reduces BXM susceptibility and compromises its clinical efficacy. Understanding the dynamics underlying resistance through computational modeling has been hindered by the complex electronic properties of the bimetallic catalytic center within the PAN active site, posing a challenge for accurate parametrization. Therefore, in this study, we systematically benchmarked metal-parametrization strategies for molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, including the nonbonded, bonded, and hybrid models, simulating wild-type PAN in both apo and drug-bound states. Identification of reliable parametrization schemes enabled MD simulations of five clinically relevant mutants, I38T/F/M, A36V, and E23K, revealing how each reshapes the conformational landscape to modulate drug-binding modes. Together, our results provide a path toward modeling complex sites in metalloenzymes and a mechanistic foundation for vulnerabilities in PAN to guide structure-based optimization of next-generation inhibitors.
papers.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 甲型流感病毒给全球带来了重大的健康负担,而 抗病毒药物 对 抗病毒药物 baloxavir marboxil (BXM) 的耐药性的迅速出现损害了其临床疗效,凸显了了解耐药动态的必要性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究系统地对野生型 PA N 末端核酸内切酶结构域 (PAN) 在 apo 和药物结合状态下的分子动力学 (MD) 模拟的金属参数化策略进行了基准测试。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员评估了非键合、键合和混合模型的参数化,并使用已确定的可靠方案对五个临床相关突变体(I38T/F/M、A36V 和 E23K)进行 MD 模拟。
elements_zh.main_results: MD 模拟揭示了每个临床相关的 突变 如何重塑构象景观以调节 PAN 活性位点的药物结合模式。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将他们的发现解释为为金属酶中的复杂位点建模提供了一条途径,并为 PAN 的脆弱性提供了机制基础,以指导下一代抑制剂的优化。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为针对 PAN 漏洞提供了机制基础,可以为针对甲型流感病毒的改进 抗病毒药物 疗法的基于结构的设计提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于计算模型,可能无法完全捕捉体内生物复杂性,但临床相关 突变 的系统基准测试和直接模拟为机制见解提供了高度可信度。

papers.abstract_zh: 甲型流感病毒通过季节性流行病和偶尔的大流行继续给全球健康和经济带来重大负担,凸显了持续开发 抗病毒药物 的迫切需要。作为抗流感疗法的最新补充,baloxavir marboxil (BXM) 以高度保守的 PA N 末端核酸内切酶结构域 (PAN) 为靶点,阻断病毒转录起始所必需的帽抢夺过程。然而,突变 耐药性的迅速出现显着降低了 BXM 的敏感性并损害了其临床疗效。PAN 活性位点内双金属催化中心复杂的电子特性阻碍了通过计算模型了解电阻的动力学,这对精确参数化提出了挑战。因此,在本研究中,我们系统地对分子动力学 (MD) 模拟的金属参数化策略进行了基准测试,包括非键合模型、键合模型和混合模型,模拟了 apo 和药物结合状态下的野生型 PAN。可靠的参数化方案的识别使得能够对五个临床相关突变体 I38T/F/M、A36V 和 E23K 进行 MD 模拟,揭示每个突变体如何重塑构象景观以调节药物结合模式。总之,我们的结果为金属酶中复杂位点的建模提供了一条途径,并为 PAN 漏洞提供了机制基础,以指导下一代抑制剂的基于结构的优化。

papers.title: Near real-time data on the human neutralizing antibody landscape to influenza virus as of early 2026 to inform vaccine-strain selection
papers.abstract: Abstract Twice each year, a decision is made on whether to update the strains included in the seasonal influenza vaccine to better match the most recent circulating viral strains. To characterize the antigenic properties of current seasonal influenza A strains to inform the upcoming decision about which strains to include in the 2026-2027 Northern Hemisphere vaccine, here we perform high-throughput sequencing-based neutralization assays using a library of 57 H3N2 and 34 H1N1 influenza hemagglutinins reflecting the circulating diversity of strains in late 2025 to early 2026. We assay this library against 302 human sera collected in late 2025. The resulting data set encompasses 27,409 titers, and provides a near real-time portrait of the human neutralizing antibody landscape against influenza virus. We find that many human sera have lower titers against the K subclade of H3N2 and the D.3.1.1 subclade of H1N1; these subclades have recently become dominant among their respective subtypes. Our measurements also reveal variability in titers to different subvariants within the K subclade of H3N2, with titers especially low to subclade K strains with additional mutations in antigenic regions D and E. We make all our data and accompanying visualizations publicly available to enable their use in vaccine-strain selection and analyses of influenza evolution and immunity.

papers.title_zh: 截至 2026 年初人类流感病毒中和抗体状况的近实时数据,为 疫苗 菌株选择提供信息
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Twice each year, a decision is made on whether to update the strains included in the seasonal influenza vaccine to better match the most recent circulating viral strains. To characterize the antigenic properties of current seasonal influenza A strains to inform the upcoming decision about which strains to include in the 2026-2027 Northern Hemisphere vaccine, here we perform high-throughput sequencing-based neutralization assays using a library of 57 H3N2 and 34 H1N1 influenza hemagglutinins reflecting the circulating diversity of strains in late 2025 to early 2026. We assay this library against 302 human sera collected in late 2025. The resulting data set encompasses 27,409 titers, and provides a near real-time portrait of the human neutralizing antibody landscape against influenza virus. We find that many human sera have lower titers against the K subclade of H3N2 and the D.3.1.1 subclade of H1N1; these subclades have recently become dominant among their respective subtypes. Our measurements also reveal variability in titers to different subvariants within the K subclade of H3N2, with titers especially low to subclade K strains with additional mutations in antigenic regions D and E. We make all our data and accompanying visualizations publicly available to enable their use in vaccine-strain selection and analyses of influenza evolution and immunity.

papers.title: When the Flu Breaks the Heart: A Case Report of Influenza A-Induced Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy
papers.abstract: We present a case of Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (TCM), commonly known as broken heart syndrome, triggered by influenza A infection. Known cardiac complications of influenza include myocardial infarction, myocarditis, and pericarditis. Only a few cases of influenza have so far been reported that led to TCM. We discuss the presentation, investigations, and management of a 67-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department (ED) with chest pain and shortness of breath two weeks after being diagnosed with influenza A. We aim to highlight a rare cardiac complication of influenza infection so that clinicians can have a high index of suspicion for this association.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Infectious Disease Surveillance: Applications, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
papers.abstract: Infectious disease surveillance is a critical component of global public health systems, enabling the detection, monitoring, and prevention of disease outbreaks. Traditional surveillance methods often rely on manual reporting and laboratory confirmation, which can lead to delays, incomplete data, and limited real-time analysis. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative approach to overcoming these limitations by enabling faster, more accurate, and data-driven surveillance systems. This article explores the role of AI in infectious disease surveillance, highlighting its applications in early outbreak detection, real-time monitoring, predictive modeling, genomic surveillance, and digital data analysis. AI technologies such as machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing allow the analysis of large and diverse datasets from sources including electronic health records, social media, mobile data, and global health databases. These systems have been effectively used in identifying early signals of outbreaks such as COVID-19, tracking disease spread during Ebola, and predicting seasonal influenza trends. Despite these advantages, challenges such as data privacy concerns, algorithmic bias, data quality issues, and infrastructure limitations in developing regions remain significant barriers. Overall, AI holds great potential to enhance global disease surveillance by improving early detection, increasing accuracy, and enabling real-time insights. With proper ethical frameworks and global collaboration, AI can play a vital role in strengthening future public health preparedness and response systems.

In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative approach to overcoming these limitations by enabling faster, more accurate, and data-driven surveillance systems. This article explores the role of AI in infectious disease surveillance, highlighting its applications in early outbreak detection, real-time monitoring, predictive modeling, genomic surveillance, and digital data analysis. AI technologies such as machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing allow the analysis of large and diverse datasets from sources including electronic health records, social media, mobile data, and global health databases. These systems have been effectively used in identifying early signals of outbreaks such as COVID-19, tracking disease spread during Ebola, and predicting seasonal influenza trends. Despite these advantages, challenges such as data privacy concerns, algorithmic bias, data quality issues, and infrastructure limitations in developing regions remain significant barriers. Overall, AI holds great potential to enhance global disease surveillance by improving early detection, increasing accuracy, and enabling real-time insights. With proper ethical frameworks and global collaboration, AI can play a vital role in strengthening future public health preparedness and response systems.
