SINCE 1978 Close the sidebar Life Sports Entertainment Food Travel Beauty & Health Fashion KT LUXE Dubai Dining Diaries Home Lifestyle Health Influenza vaccine in UAE: When is best time to get shots ahead of back-to-school? The seasonal flu vaccine is suitable for all ages, starting from six months old, and is strongly recommended for everyone in the community Published: Mon 27 Jul 2026, 1:49 PM By Ruqayya Al Qaydi Follow us Follow on Google Follow on WhatsApp Follow on Telegram As the back-to-school season approaches, UAE health experts are urging parents to prioritise the seasonal influenza vaccine alongside their back-to-school shopping, emphasising that early vaccination is crucial to protect children and the wider community from the flu virus. With students preparing to return to classrooms, doctors stress that September is the ideal time to get the flu shot, as it takes up to two weeks for the body to build immunity.Importance of early vaccination Dr Mansoor Anwar Habib, Consultant in Family Medicine and Occupational Health, highlighted the critical role of the seasonal flu vaccine in mitigating the severity of the illness. “The flu vaccine does not completely prevent the disease, but it significantly reduces the severity of the symptoms if a person is infected,” Dr Habib explained. Dr Mansoor Anwar Habib, Consultant in Family Medicine and Occupational Health By familiarising the immune system with the viral strains included in the annual vaccine, the body is better prepared to fight off the virus. “If the virus enters the body after vaccination, the immune system recognises it immediately and can handle it, resulting in much milder symptoms,” he noted. This reduction in symptom severity also plays a vital role in curbing the spread of the virus. “Because the vaccine lessens the symptoms, it consequently reduces the likelihood of transmitting the infection from one person to another,” Dr Habib added.Timing is everything Timing is a critical factor in the effectiveness of the flu vaccine. Dr Habib strongly advised taking the vaccine in early to mid-September, or as soon as it becomes available at health centres and hospitals. “It takes about two weeks for the vaccine to become effective. With the start of schools and the increased risk of spreading infections, the earlier one gets vaccinated, the better,” he stated. While availability may vary sometimes — arriving in early, mid, or late September depending on the healthcare facility — the overarching message is to act promptly. As parents prepare for the new academic year, buying uniforms and stationery is often on the top of ones mind. However, Dr Habib urged families to add the flu vaccine to their checklist. “Just as parents remember to buy school supplies for their children, they should also remember to vaccinate their children and themselves,” he emphasised. The seasonal flu vaccine is suitable for all ages, starting from six months old, and is strongly recommended for everyone in the community. Dr Habib further noted that the vaccine will be available at health centres and hospitals from the beginning of September onwards.Broader community protection The call for early vaccination aligns with broader health guidelines in the UAE. The Ministry of Health and Prevention (MoHap) consistently advocates for annual flu vaccinations, particularly for high-risk groups, including young children, the elderly, pregnant women, and individuals with chronic medical conditions. Recent studies have underscored the impact of pediatric flu vaccines. Research from Harvard Medical School found that vaccinating children aged two to five can reduce infection rates by up to 14 per cent, highlighting children as key transmitters of the virus due to their time spent in close-contact environments like schools and nurseries. By ensuring children are vaccinated, parents not only protect their own families but also contribute to a healthier community, reducing missed school days and hospital visits during the peak flu season. Dr Habib call to action for all residents: “We recommend everyone in the community get vaccinated. The vaccine will be available at health centres and hospitals from the beginning of September onwards.” ALSO READ: Back-to-school bugs: UAE doctors warn parents not to ignore these signs ‘1 missed vaccine can be life-threatening’: UAE doctors back Dh20,000 fine plan Second peak of flu season in UAE? Doctors say never too late to get vaccinated Ruqayya Al Qaydi Ruqayya Alqaydi is a Special Correspondent with an endless curiosity to learn. Like a journalist on... More ralqaydi@khaleejtimes.com

news.source_body_en: As the back-to-school season approaches in the UAE, health experts are urging parents to prioritize the seasonal influenza vaccine for their children and themselves. Dr. Mansoor Anwar Habib, a consultant in Family Medicine and Occupational Health, emphasizes that September is the ideal time to get vaccinated, as it takes up to two weeks for the body to build immunity. While the vaccine does not completely prevent the flu, it significantly reduces symptom severity and transmission risk. The vaccine is suitable for all ages starting from six months and is strongly recommended for everyone, particularly high-risk groups. news.content: Share the news iNDICA NEWS BUREAU- Scientists have created the first detailed map showing how the influenza A virus takes control of human cells during infection, a breakthrough that could help researchers develop better flu drugs and vaccines. The study, published in the peer-reviewed journal Nature Microbiology, was led by researchers at EMBL Hamburg in collaboration with scientists from the Leibniz Research Institute for Molecular Pharmacology (FMP), Charite – Universitatsmedizin Berlin, and other research partners. It provides the first large-scale structural map of direct interactions between influenza A virus proteins and human cell proteins inside intact infected cells. Seasonal influenza causes up to 650,000 deaths worldwide every year and leads to severe illness in an estimated 3 million to 5 million people. Influenza A has also caused several pandemics, including the 1918 Spanish Flu. To carry out the research, scientists developed a customized workflow that allowed them to observe how viral and human proteins interact directly inside infected cells. They used a specialized version of cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS), adapted specifically for virus-infected cells. The technique enabled them to capture short-lived and location-specific protein interactions that earlier methods often failed to detect. The researchers then combined the XL-MS data with a modified version of AlphaFold, the artificial intelligence-based protein structure prediction tool. This helped them build detailed models showing how viral and human proteins physically interact inside infected cells. The study revealed two major ways influenza A hijacks human cells. One involved the virus’s surface protein, hemagglutinin, which relies on host proteins as it moves through the cell’s transport and processing system. These host proteins help fold and modify the viral protein, allowing the virus to continue its infection process. The researchers also discovered that influenza A causes paraspeckles, small droplet-like structures inside the cell nucleus, to break apart during infection. This releases RNA-binding proteins that the virus can use to support its own replication. The team found this effect consistently across different human cell lines and influenza strains, suggesting it is part of the virus’s infection strategy rather than a random side effect. Scientists believe disrupting paraspeckles may also weaken the cell’s natural defense mechanisms, making it easier for the virus to multiply. The research brought together scientific expertise and facilities from several institutions. Cross-linking mass spectrometry experiments were carried out at Charite in Berlin, glycoproteomics analyses were conducted at the EMBL Proteomics Core Facility, AlphaFold modeling was performed on the EMBL Compute Cluster, and microscopy imaging was completed at the Centre for Structural Systems Biology’s Advanced Light and Fluorescence Microscopy Facility. The researchers said the approach could be used to study many other viruses, not just influenza. They believe the combination of in-cell cross-linking, structural modeling, and cell biology can help scientists understand how different viruses interact with human cells during infection. The team also said the method could be applied to viruses with pandemic potential, including H5N1 bird flu, to identify the interaction networks that help them multiply inside human cells and uncover new targets for future antiviral treatments. Photo: Dmytro Vynohradov/ Unsplash

news.content_title: Most Americans Unaware of CDC's Pregnancy Vaccine Recommendations
news.content: Most Americans are unaware or unsure which vaccines the CDC recommends during pregnancy, according to a nationally representative survey of US adults released July 22, 2026, by the Annenberg Public Policy Center (APPC) of the University of Pennsylvania. 1 A new survey shows widespread uncertainty about which vaccines the CDC recommends during pregnancy, underscoring the counseling role pharmacists play. | Image Credit: Marina Demidiuk - stock.adobe.com The survey, fielded July 1 to 5, 2026, among 1031 US adults, found that even the best-known recommendation—the seasonal flu vaccine—was correctly identified by less than half of respondents. 1 The findings raise questions for pharmacists, who administer a substantial share of vaccinations and are often the last clinical touchpoint before a pregnant patient decides whether to vaccinate. Awareness of Recommended Vaccines Is Low According to CDC guidance, 4 vaccines are routinely recommended during pregnancy: the seasonal influenza vaccine; the Tdap vaccine (tetanus, diphtheria, and pertussis), preferably between 27 and 36 weeks' gestation; the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine, given during weeks 32 to 36 in RSV season; and the hepatitis B vaccine for those not already vaccinated. Among all adults surveyed, awareness of these recommendations ranged from 23% for the hepatitis B vaccine to 48% for the seasonal flu vaccine. 1 For the COVID-19 vaccine, more than half of respondents did not know whether the CDC recommends it. The agency's current guidance frames COVID-19 vaccination during pregnancy as a matter of individual decision-making rather than a routine recommendation, a position the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) has said does not go far enough, as ACOG "continues to recommend that all pregnant and lactating individuals receive an updated COVID-19 vaccine." 1 Women aged 18 to 49 years were significantly more knowledgeable than other adults on most items, correctly identifying the hepatitis B vaccine recommendation 30% of the time and the flu vaccine recommendation 60% of the time, compared with 21% and 43%, respectively, among other adults. Awareness of the RSV vaccine recommendation did not differ significantly between the 2 groups. 2 Uncertainty Dominates the Findings Across every vaccine the CDC recommends during pregnancy, plus the COVID-19 vaccine, "not sure" was the most common response. Between 45% and 66% of all adults said they were not sure whether the CDC recommends the flu, Tdap, RSV, hepatitis B, or COVID-19 vaccines during pregnancy. analysis.brief_en: A new survey reveals widespread uncertainty among Americans about CDC-recommended vaccines during pregnancy, with awareness ranging from 23% to 48% for key vaccines. Conducted July 1-5, 2026, among 1,031 US adults, the Annenberg Public Policy Center study found that 'not sure' was the most common response across all recommended vaccines, including seasonal flu, Tdap, RSV, and hepatitis B. Women of childbearing age showed slightly higher awareness but still significant uncertainty. The findings underscore the critical role of pharmacists as counselors, particularly amid evolving federal guidance and professional society recommendations that are not always aligned. The survey highlights challenges in public health communication during a period of policy flux.

news.content: Amid the rising cases of swine flu reported in the month of July, Nagpur has reported the first death from Influenza A (H1N1) this year. As per reports, nearly 25 cases of the H1N1 virus have been reported in Nagpur since the beginning of the year. However, the swine flu is considered a seasonal viral infection now and not a pandemic, thus eliminating the cause of worry and panic. Most people affected by the virus recover within a week of being infected, while some develop severe complications. The H1N1 virus is a contagious flu that is transmitted through infected people. It mainly spreads through respiratory droplets released when an infected person coughs, sneezes or talks. While the symptoms can mimic those of a common cold and cough, it is important to recognise the correct symptoms early to know when to consult a doctor. The symptoms of H1N1 are similar to those of seasonal influenza and usually appear one to four days after exposure to the virus. Some of the most common signs, as per Mayo Clinic, include: High fever or chills Persistent cough Sore throat Runny or blocked nose Headache Body and muscle aches Extreme tiredness or fatigue Sneezing Vomiting and diarrhoea, particularly in children, though adults may experience them as well. Although mild cases can often be managed at home with adequate rest, hydration and medications prescribed by a healthcare provider, certain warning signs require immediate medical attention. Seek medical care if you experience: Difficulty breathing or shortness of breath Persistent chest pain or pressure Bluish lips or fingertips High fever that does not improve or returns after subsiding Severe dizziness, confusion or difficulty staying awake Persistent vomiting leading to dehydration Symptoms that worsen instead of improving after a few days People at higher risk of severe illness include young children, adults aged 65 years and above, pregnant women, individuals with weakened immunity, and those with chronic conditions such as diabetes, asthma, heart disease or kidney disorders. analysis.brief_en: In July 2026, Nagpur reported the first death from Influenza A (H1N1) this year, with 25 cases recorded since January. The outbreak is described as seasonal, not pandemic-related. Symptoms include fever, cough, sore throat, and body aches, typically appearing 1-4 days post-exposure. While most recover within a week, severe cases may require medical attention, particularly for high-risk groups like young children, elderly, pregnant women, and those with chronic conditions. The virus spreads through respiratory droplets, emphasizing the importance of early symptom recognition and timely medical consultation.

news.content_title: Nat Microbiol:流感病毒如何“劫持”人细胞?科学家绘制出一张分子级别的入侵地图 - 生物研究专区 - 生物谷
news.content: 资讯 生物在线 品牌会议 行云公开课 登录 注册 生物谷APP 搜索 最新会议 空中讲坛 热点推荐 生物在线 资讯 生物在线 品牌会议 行云公开课 活动集锦 ePoch专访 企业库 疾病库 投资库 期刊学会 热点事件 园区报道 打开APP 首页 生物研究 详情页 Nat Microbiol:流感病毒如何“劫持”人细胞?科学家绘制出一张分子级别的入侵地图 血凝素 甲型流感病毒 无膜细胞器 细胞内交联 来源:生物谷原创 2026-07-24 11:00 科学家们通过研究首次在完整感染细胞内,以近原子尺度的结构分辨率,绘制了甲型流感病毒与人类宿主蛋白之间的直接接触图谱。 每年全球有高达65万人死于季节性流感,另有300万至500万人因此患上严重疾病。大流行毒株的威胁更为严峻—1918年西班牙大流感、2009年甲型H1N1大流行,都曾在短时间内席卷全球。流感病毒之所以难缠,不仅在于其表面抗原频繁变异,更在于它侵入宿主细胞后,能够熟练地“策反”细胞的分子机器,将其变为病毒复制的工厂。然而,病毒与宿主蛋白之间究竟在何处、以何种方式直接“交手”,此前一直缺乏系统性的全景视图。 日前,一篇发表在国际杂志Nature Microbiology上题为“Mapping in-cell protein contact sites reveals hijacking of paraspeckles during influenza A virus infection”的研究报告中,来自欧洲分子生物学实验室等机构的科学家们通过研究首次在完整感染细胞内,以近原子尺度的结构分辨率,绘制了甲型流感病毒与人类宿主蛋白之间的直接接触图谱。这项研究不仅发现了多个此前未知的病毒-宿主相互作用位点,更揭示了两条清晰的病毒操控路径:一条发生在细胞质的膜性运输系统中,另一条则直击细胞核内的无膜细胞器。 文章中,研究人员采用的核心技术是经过特殊优化的细胞内交联质谱联用技术。传统方法需要先破碎细胞再检测蛋白互作,这极易产生“假阳性”——原本在完整细胞中永不相见的蛋白,可能在试管中意外相遇;而脆弱或依赖于特定空间位置的接触,又极易丢失。新型交联质谱技术则能在细胞保持完整的状态下,将空间上邻近的蛋白“锁定”并加以识别。配合改良版的AlphaFold结构预测算法,实验数据被直接输入模型,指导预测病毒与宿主蛋白复合体的三维构型。这种“实验+计算”的闭环策略,大大提升了预测可靠性,尤其对于进化上高度动态的病毒-宿主互作界面,效果尤为显著。 甲型流感病毒感染过程中的细胞内交联 该研究的第一条重要发现,围绕病毒表面关键蛋白—血凝素,血凝素负责识别并入侵宿主细胞,但其本身必须经过宿主内质网-高尔基体膜性系统的精确修饰与折叠,才能具备感染活性。借助交联质谱,研究人员系统追踪了血凝素在分泌通路中的“旅行轨迹”,并鉴定了与之发生直接接触的多个宿主蛋白。其中部分宿主因子此前从未被关联到病毒感染过程。这些蛋白像流水线上的质检员与装配工,协助病毒蛋白完成特定糖基化修饰,使其成熟为具备功能的构象。这一结果精准定位了病毒“借用”宿主蛋白加工体系的节点,也为设计干扰血凝素成熟的抗病毒药物提供了明确靶点。 更令人意外的发现来自细胞核内,研究人员观察到,感染甲型流感病毒后,核内一种名为“副斑点”的无膜细胞器发生了系统性、不可逆的解体。副斑点属于相分离凝聚体,内部富集了多种RNA结合蛋白和长链非编码RNA,被认为参与基因调控和应激反应。在多个细胞系、多种流感毒株的测试中,这一解体现象均稳定出现,提示这并非感染的副产物,而更像一种病毒精心策划的策略。进一步的机制解析表明,病毒至少动用了三把“钥匙”来打开副斑点:病毒核蛋白和非结构蛋白1直接与副斑点核心组分发生物理接触;病毒内切酶PA-X则负责降解副斑点内关键的长链非编码RNA;同时,病毒聚合酶对宿主RNA聚合酶II的抑制,进一步加剧了解体进程。副斑点瓦解后,原本被束缚其中的RNA结合蛋白被释放,这些游离的宿主因子随即被病毒招募,转而促进病毒自身的转录与复制。换言之,病毒不仅拆掉了细胞核内的“应激堡垒”,还顺手将里面的“守军”收缴改编为己用。 研究人员强调,这套“细胞内交联-结构建模-功能验证”的组合拳,完全可应用于其他具有大流行潜力的病毒,例如高致病性禽流感H5N1。在真实感染场景下原位捕捉分子接触,不仅能让科学家看清病毒如何“动手”,更能揭示哪些蛋白间的握手指尖最脆弱、最易被药物介入打断。对于长期困扰人类的流感病毒而言,一张精细的分子劫持地图,或许正是通往下一代抗病毒策略的必经之路。(生物谷Bioon.com) 参考文献: Kotova, I., Mühlberg, L., Gilep, K. et al. news.content_original: 资讯 生物在线 品牌会议 行云公开课 登录 注册 生物谷APP 搜索 最新会议 空中讲坛 热点推荐 生物在线 资讯 生物在线 品牌会议 行云公开课 活动集锦 ePoch专访 企业库 疾病库 投资库 期刊学会 热点事件 园区报道 打开APP 首页 生物研究 详情页 Nat Microbiol:流感病毒如何“劫持”人细胞?科学家绘制出一张分子级别的入侵地图 血凝素 甲型流感病毒 无膜细胞器 细胞内交联 来源:生物谷原创 2026-07-24 11:00 科学家们通过研究首次在完整感染细胞内,以近原子尺度的结构分辨率,绘制了甲型流感病毒与人类宿主蛋白之间的直接接触图谱。 每年全球有高达65万人死于季节性流感,另有300万至500万人因此患上严重疾病。大流行毒株的威胁更为严峻—1918年西班牙大流感、2009年甲型H1N1大流行,都曾在短时间内席卷全球。流感病毒之所以难缠,不仅在于其表面抗原频繁变异,更在于它侵入宿主细胞后,能够熟练地“策反”细胞的分子机器,将其变为病毒复制的工厂。然而,病毒与宿主蛋白之间究竟在何处、以何种方式直接“交手”,此前一直缺乏系统性的全景视图。 日前,一篇发表在国际杂志Nature Microbiology上题为“Mapping in-cell protein contact sites reveals hijacking of paraspeckles during influenza A virus infection”的研究报告中,来自欧洲分子生物学实验室等机构的科学家们通过研究首次在完整感染细胞内,以近原子尺度的结构分辨率,绘制了甲型流感病毒与人类宿主蛋白之间的直接接触图谱。这项研究不仅发现了多个此前未知的病毒-宿主相互作用位点,更揭示了两条清晰的病毒操控路径:一条发生在细胞质的膜性运输系统中,另一条则直击细胞核内的无膜细胞器。 文章中,研究人员采用的核心技术是经过特殊优化的细胞内交联质谱联用技术。传统方法需要先破碎细胞再检测蛋白互作,这极易产生“假阳性”——原本在完整细胞中永不相见的蛋白,可能在试管中意外相遇;而脆弱或依赖于特定空间位置的接触,又极易丢失。新型交联质谱技术则能在细胞保持完整的状态下,将空间上邻近的蛋白“锁定”并加以识别。配合改良版的AlphaFold结构预测算法,实验数据被直接输入模型,指导预测病毒与宿主蛋白复合体的三维构型。这种“实验+计算”的闭环策略,大大提升了预测可靠性,尤其对于进化上高度动态的病毒-宿主互作界面,效果尤为显著。 甲型流感病毒感染过程中的细胞内交联 该研究的第一条重要发现,围绕病毒表面关键蛋白—血凝素,血凝素负责识别并入侵宿主细胞,但其本身必须经过宿主内质网-高尔基体膜性系统的精确修饰与折叠,才能具备感染活性。借助交联质谱,研究人员系统追踪了血凝素在分泌通路中的“旅行轨迹”,并鉴定了与之发生直接接触的多个宿主蛋白。其中部分宿主因子此前从未被关联到病毒感染过程。这些蛋白像流水线上的质检员与装配工,协助病毒蛋白完成特定糖基化修饰,使其成熟为具备功能的构象。这一结果精准定位了病毒“借用”宿主蛋白加工体系的节点,也为设计干扰血凝素成熟的抗病毒药物提供了明确靶点。 更令人意外的发现来自细胞核内,研究人员观察到,感染甲型流感病毒后,核内一种名为“副斑点”的无膜细胞器发生了系统性、不可逆的解体。副斑点属于相分离凝聚体,内部富集了多种RNA结合蛋白和长链非编码RNA,被认为参与基因调控和应激反应。在多个细胞系、多种流感毒株的测试中,这一解体现象均稳定出现,提示这并非感染的副产物,而更像一种病毒精心策划的策略。进一步的机制解析表明,病毒至少动用了三把“钥匙”来打开副斑点:病毒核蛋白和非结构蛋白1直接与副斑点核心组分发生物理接触;病毒内切酶PA-X则负责降解副斑点内关键的长链非编码RNA;同时,病毒聚合酶对宿主RNA聚合酶II的抑制,进一步加剧了解体进程。副斑点瓦解后,原本被束缚其中的RNA结合蛋白被释放,这些游离的宿主因子随即被病毒招募,转而促进病毒自身的转录与复制。换言之,病毒不仅拆掉了细胞核内的“应激堡垒”,还顺手将里面的“守军”收缴改编为己用。 研究人员强调,这套“细胞内交联-结构建模-功能验证”的组合拳,完全可应用于其他具有大流行潜力的病毒,例如高致病性禽流感H5N1。在真实感染场景下原位捕捉分子接触,不仅能让科学家看清病毒如何“动手”,更能揭示哪些蛋白间的握手指尖最脆弱、最易被药物介入打断。对于长期困扰人类的流感病毒而言,一张精细的分子劫持地图,或许正是通往下一代抗病毒策略的必经之路。(生物谷Bioon.com) 参考文献: Kotova, I., Mühlberg, L., Gilep, K. et al. analysis.brief_en: Scientists have created a molecular-level map of how influenza A virus hijacks human cells, published in Nature Microbiology. Using advanced in-cell cross-linking mass spectrometry and improved AlphaFold predictions, researchers mapped direct contact sites between viral and host proteins at near-atomic resolution. The study reveals two key viral hijacking pathways: one in the cytoplasmic membrane transport system and another targeting nuclear membraneless organelles called paraspeckles. The research identifies previously unknown virus-host interaction sites and provides precise targets for antiviral drugs that could disrupt viral protein maturation or prevent the disassembly of paraspeckles. This 'cellular hijacking map' offers a foundation for next-generation antiviral strategies against influenza and potentially other pandemic viruses.

news.content: 基于整篇论文,可整理如下: **一种整合计算与体外研究揭示靶向甲型流感病毒RNA依赖性RNA聚合酶的新型香豆素杂化物** 《European Journal of Medicinal Chemistry》:Integrated In silico and In vitro Approaches Reveal Novel Coumarin Hybrids Targeting Influenza A Virus RNA-dependent RNA polymerase 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年07月22日 来源:European Journal of Medicinal Chemistry 6.7 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Research article Open access **摘要:** 甲型流感病毒(Influenza A virus, IAV)是引发季节性流行和大流行的主要病原体之一,且由于其高突变率,现有疫苗与抗病毒药物的保护效力常受限制。RNA依赖性RNA聚合酶(RdRp)复合体由PB1、PB2和PA亚基组成,是病毒基因组转录与复制的核心酶复合体,也是极具潜力的抗病毒靶点。研究人员基于自建化合物库LaSMMed Chemical Library(LMCL),通过分子对接虚拟筛选获得候选抑制剂,并进一步开展细胞毒性、抗病毒活性、作用机制和分子动力学模拟等研究,以评估其作为IAV抑制剂的潜力。结果显示,LMed 99与LMed 93对H1N1表现出最强活性,并对高致病性H5N1同样具有抑制作用;二者均可降低病毒RNA和蛋白表达,其中LMed 99还可降低mRNA水平。构效关系分析提示,儿茶酚结构(catechol)和卤素取代基有助于增强抗病毒效力。研究表明,这两种香豆素-酚酸杂化物可作为后续优化的新型先导化合物。 **论文解读:** 点击下载义翘神州高质量细胞培养用细胞因子,满足您药物开发的各个阶段! 领 取 本研究围绕自建化学库LMCL展开,采用虚拟筛选优先识别可同时作用于PA–PB1界面与PB2亚基的候选分子,并在体外进一步验证其细胞毒性与抗病毒效应。研究人员最终筛选出11个化合物进入生物学评价,其中多数为香豆素-酚酸杂化物。随后通过合成、表征和机制实验,重点确认LMed 93与LMed 99具有更优的抗H1N1和H5N1活性,并结合分子对接与分子动力学模拟解析其潜在作用模式。该研究的意义在于:一方面为香豆素骨架的抗流感开发提供了明确的结构优化方向;另一方面为靶向流感病毒聚合酶复合体的先导化合物筛选提供了可验证的整合研究范式。 **主要技术方法概括:** 研究主要采用虚拟筛选与分子对接、化合物合成与结构表征、MDCK II细胞中的细胞毒性与抗病毒剂量反应实验、时间加药实验、Western blot、RT-qPCR、mini-replicon双荧光素酶实验、VSV-H1N1假型入侵模型、膜融合实验以及分子动力学模拟与MM-PBSA自由能计算。样本来源为MDCK II细胞及IAV H1N1(A/WSN/1933)和H5N1(A/Thailand/KAN-1/2004)病毒株。 **研究结果:** **3.1 虚拟筛选发现潜在的H1N1聚合酶抑制剂** 通过对LMCL中116个配体构象进行对接筛选,研究人员在PA–PB1界面与PB2帽结合位点识别出20个高分化合物,其中8个同时出现在两个靶点的前列。最终进入体外验证的11个化合物中,以香豆素-酚酸杂化物为主,提示该骨架对聚合酶相关靶点具有较强适配性。 **3.2 香豆素-酚酸杂化物的合成** 研究人员合成了10个杂化物,其中6个为新化合物,并完成了熔点、NMR、FTIR、UFLC-UV及元素分析等表征。结果证明这些化合物结构明确、纯度可靠,可用于后续生物学评价。 **3.3 体外抗病毒筛选** MTT实验显示,多数含儿茶酚型二羟基取代的化合物具有更高细胞毒性,而LMed 93与LMed 99兼具较低细胞毒性和较强抗病毒活性。对H1N1筛选中,LMed 99和LMed 93分别表现出最优EC 50 与较高选择指数,成为后续机制研究重点;构效关系分析提示,酚环儿茶酚取代和香豆素环氯取代可增强抗病毒效力与选择性。 **3.4 LMed 99与LMed 93对H1N1的抑制具有时间依赖性** VSV-H1N1假型进入实验与膜融合实验均未见明显抑制,说明两者并不主要作用于病毒入侵阶段。时间加药实验表明,LMed 99在感染后1、3、6小时均可显著抑制复制,而LMed 93主要在早期与中期阶段更有效,提示二者主要作用于入侵后阶段,且LMed 99可能具有更持续的细胞内效应。 **3.5 LMed 99与LMed 93降低vRNA积累,但对mRNA的影响不同** RT-qPCR结果显示,两种化合物均可显著降低M1 vRNA水平,提示其均影响病毒基因组复制。LMed 99在早期还可显著降低M1与PB1 mRNA,而LMed 93虽明显抑制vRNA,却未显著影响mRNA水平,说明两者对转录与复制的调控并不完全一致。 **3.6 LMed 99与LMed 93可时间依赖性降低病毒蛋白表达** Western blot显示,LMed 93在早期可降低PB1、PA、PB2、NP和M1蛋白,但随给药延后作用减弱;LMed 99则在1 hpi和3 hpi对多种病毒蛋白均有明显抑制,6 hpi时仅M1仍保持显著下降。该结果与RNA水平变化总体一致,支持其干扰病毒复制后期事件。 **3.7 两种化合物对聚合酶活性的调控存在差异** mini-replicon实验表明,LMed 93可中度降低聚合酶相关报告活性,而LMed 99却提高了报告信号。该结果与感染体系中的抗病毒效应不完全一致,提示其作用机制并不能仅以该简化体系中的聚合酶读数解释。 **3.8 99可在PA–PB1界面形成多重氢键、疏水作用及卤素相互作用;在PB2位点则与若干关键残基形成氢键和疏水接触。结果支持其可能通过影响聚合酶复合体装配或帽结合功能发挥作用。 **3.10 分子动力学模拟与自由能分析支持PA–PB1为优先靶点** 200 93主要在早期与中期阶段更有效,提示二者主要作用于入侵后阶段,且LMed 99可能具有更持续的细胞内效应。 **3.5 LMed 99与LMed 93降低vRNA积累,但对mRNA的影响不同** RT-qPCR结果显示,两种化合物均可显著降低M1 vRNA水平,提示其均影响病毒基因组复制。LMed 99在早期还可显著降低M1与PB1 mRNA,而LMed 93虽明显抑制vRNA,却未显著影响mRNA水平,说明两者对转录与复制的调控并不完全一致。 **3.6 LMed 99与LMed 93可时间依赖性降低病毒蛋白表达** Western blot显示,LMed 93在早期可降低PB1、PA、PB2、NP和M1蛋白,但随给药延后作用减弱;LMed 99则在1 hpi和3 hpi对多种病毒蛋白均有明显抑制,6 analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: In vitro study; no human cases or outbreaks reported. Compounds showed potent inhibition of H1N1 and H5N1 viruses with EC50 values of 4.9 μM (LMed 99) and 9.13 μM (LMed 93) for H5N1. No direct risk assessment provided.

analysis.brief_en: A new study published in the European Journal of Medicinal Chemistry identifies two novel coumarin hybrids, LMed 93 and LMed 99, as potent inhibitors of influenza A virus (IAV) RNA-dependent RNA polymerase. Through computational screening and in vitro validation, these compounds demonstrated strong activity against both H1N1 and H5N1 strains, reducing viral RNA and protein expression. The research suggests these hybrids target the PA-PB1 interface of the viral polymerase complex, offering a promising lead for developing broad-spectrum anti-influenza drugs. While the study provides a robust framework for antiviral discovery, further research is needed to confirm direct molecular targets and evaluate in vivo efficacy.

news.source_body_en: A new study published in the European Journal of Medicinal Chemistry identifies two novel coumarin hybrids, LMed 93 and LMed 99, as potent inhibitors of influenza A virus (IAV) RNA-dependent RNA polymerase. Through computational screening and in vitro validation, these compounds demonstrated strong activity against both H1N1 and H5N1 strains, reducing viral RNA and protein expression. The research suggests these hybrids target the PA-PB1 interface of the viral polymerase complex, offering a promising lead for developing broad-spectrum anti-influenza drugs. While the study provides a robust framework for antiviral discovery, further research is needed to confirm direct molecular targets and evaluate in vivo efficacy.
news.content_zh: 发表在《欧洲药物化学杂志》上的一项新研究确定了两种新型香豆素杂合体 LMed 93 和 LMed 99,它们是甲型流感病毒 (IAV) RNA 依赖性 RNA 聚合酶的有效抑制剂。通过计算筛选和体外验证,这些化合物对 H1N1 和 H5N1 病毒株表现出强大的活性,可减少病毒 RNA 和蛋白质表达。研究表明,这些杂交体靶向病毒聚合酶复合物的 PA-PB1 界面,为开发广谱抗流感药物提供了有希望的先导。虽然该研究为 抗病毒药物 的发现提供了强大的框架,但仍需要进一步的研究来确认直接分子靶标并评估体内功效。

news.wechat_summary_zh: 时间：发表于2026-07-22；在此日期之前进行的研究。；地点与对象：证据中未注明；使用 MDCK II 细胞和 IAV H1N1 (A/WSN/1933) 和 H5N1 (A/Thailand/KAN-1/2004) 病毒株进行体外研究。；事件：发表在《欧洲药物化学杂志》上的研究描述了针对甲型流感病毒 RNA 依赖性 RNA 聚合酶的新型香豆素杂合体(LMed 93 和 LMed 99)，并通过计算和体外研究得到证实。；影响与风险：体外研究；没有人类病例或 暴发 的报告。化合物对 H1N1 和 H5N1 病毒具有有效抑制作用，对 H5N1 病毒的 EC50 值为 4.9 μM (LMed 99) 和 9.13 μM (LMed 93)。...；应对与不确定性：研究属于临床前研究；没有公共卫生反应或调查的报告。尽管有计算和实验证据，但研究的局限性包括依赖体外模型和未解决的分子靶标。
